name: aggregate-root
summary: An aggregate that holds entities has exactly one root.
explanation: The root is the record the aggregate is named for, through which its other entities are reached (FORMAT.md section 16). An aggregate with no entities is not reported. Give exactly one of its entities `role: root`.
query:
SELECT 'error' AS severity, 'aggregate-root' AS "check", a.id AS record,
       CASE WHEN a.roots = 0
         THEN 'Aggregate ' || a.id || ' has entities but no root; set role: root on the entity the aggregate is named for.'
         ELSE 'Aggregate ' || a.id || ' has ' || a.roots || ' root entities, ' || a.root_ids
              || '; keep one as root and set role: child on the others.'
       END AS message
FROM (
  SELECT g.id,
         count(DISTINCT e.path) FILTER (WHERE lower(trim(f.value)) = 'root') AS roots,
         string_agg(DISTINCT e.id, ', ' ORDER BY e.id) FILTER (WHERE lower(trim(f.value)) = 'root') AS root_ids
  FROM records g
  JOIN records e ON e.parent = g.id AND e.kind = 'entity'
  LEFT JOIN fields f ON f.path = e.path AND f.name = 'role'
  WHERE g.kind = 'aggregate' AND g.id <> ''
  GROUP BY g.id
) a
WHERE a.roots <> 1
ORDER BY record

name: applies-when-unknown
summary: A pattern rule's `applies_when` is well formed and names one of its pattern's settings.
explanation: A pattern rule that applies only for some values of a setting says so in `applies_when`, written `<setting> is <value>` or `<setting> is not <value>`; it is then waived in each domain where no follower (a following use case, or the domain when it follows the pattern itself) gives that setting a value that meets it. A malformed field, or one naming a setting the pattern does not list, waives nothing. A rule whose parent is not a pattern is reported by the parent checks instead. Write the field as `<setting> is <value>` with one of the pattern's settings, add the setting to the pattern, or remove the field.
query:
SELECT DISTINCT 'error' AS severity, 'applies-when-unknown' AS "check", nullif(r.id, '') AS record,
       'Pattern rule ' || coalesce(nullif(r.id, ''), r.path) || ' says it applies when "' || trim(aw.value) || '", '
       || CASE WHEN NOT regexp_full_match(trim(aw.value), '(?is)\S+\s+is\s+\S.*')
               THEN 'which is not written as "<setting> is <value>" or "<setting> is not <value>".'
               ELSE 'but pattern ' || p.id || ' has no setting "' || regexp_extract(trim(aw.value), '(?is)^(\S+)\s+is\s', 1) || '"; '
                    || CASE WHEN trim(coalesce(ps.value, '')) = '' THEN 'it has no settings.' ELSE 'its settings are: ' || trim(ps.value) || '.' END
          END AS message
FROM records r
JOIN fields aw ON aw.path = r.path AND aw.name = 'applies_when'
JOIN records p ON p.id = r.parent AND p.kind = 'pattern'
LEFT JOIN fields ps ON ps.path = p.path AND ps.name = 'settings'
WHERE r.kind = 'pattern_rule' AND trim(aw.value) <> ''
  AND (NOT regexp_full_match(trim(aw.value), '(?is)\S+\s+is\s+\S.*')
       OR NOT list_contains(string_split_regex(trim(coalesce(ps.value, '')), '\s+'),
                            regexp_extract(trim(aw.value), '(?is)^(\S+)\s+is\s', 1)))
ORDER BY record, message

name: bad-id
summary: Every record has an ID in the form `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*(-[A-Z0-9]+)*$`.
explanation: An ID is capital letters and digits, starting with a letter, in parts joined by single hyphens, such as `TL-LEND-UC01`. A record with no ID, or with lower-case letters, spaces or other signs in it, is reported. Rewrite the ID in that form, following the ID convention for its kind.
query:
SELECT 'error' AS severity, 'bad-id' AS "check", nullif(id, '') AS record,
       CASE WHEN id = '' THEN path || ' has no id.'
            ELSE 'ID ' || id || ' (in ' || path || ') does not match the ID format: capital letters and digits in parts joined by hyphens, starting with a letter.'
       END AS message
FROM records
WHERE NOT regexp_full_match(id, '[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*(-[A-Z0-9]+)*')
ORDER BY path

name: bad-pattern-settings
summary: A pattern's settings are field names a use case can carry.
explanation: A field name is lower-case letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter, and not one of the fields every record has (`id`, `kind`, `title`, `parent`, `links`). A missing settings field is missing-required-field. Rename the setting in the pattern's `settings` list.
query:
SELECT DISTINCT 'error' AS severity, 'bad-pattern-settings' AS "check", nullif(p.id, '') AS record,
       'Pattern ' || coalesce(nullif(p.id, ''), p.path) || ' has setting "' || s.name || '", which is not a valid field name'
       || CASE WHEN s.name IN ('id', 'kind', 'title', 'parent', 'links') THEN ': every record already has it.'
               ELSE ': use lower-case letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter.' END AS message
FROM records p
JOIN fields f ON f.path = p.path AND f.name = 'settings'
CROSS JOIN unnest(string_split_regex(trim(f.value), '\s+')) AS s(name)
WHERE p.kind = 'pattern' AND s.name <> ''
  AND (NOT regexp_full_match(s.name, '[a-z][a-z0-9_]*') OR s.name IN ('id', 'kind', 'title', 'parent', 'links'))
ORDER BY record, message

name: bad-test-state
summary: A test's state, when given, is automated, manual or planned.
explanation: The state is read in any letter case, as coverage reads it. Without a state a test is automated. Fix the value, or remove the field for an automated test.
query:
SELECT 'error' AS severity, 'bad-test-state' AS "check", nullif(r.id, '') AS record,
       'Test ' || coalesce(nullif(r.id, ''), r.path) || ' has state "' || f.value
       || '"; a test''s state must be automated, manual or planned.' AS message
FROM records r
JOIN fields f ON f.path = r.path AND f.name = 'state'
WHERE r.kind = 'test' AND trim(f.value) <> '' AND lower(trim(f.value)) NOT IN ('automated', 'manual', 'planned')
ORDER BY r.path

name: capability-order
summary: A capability's order is a whole number that no other capability in its domain has.
explanation: Orders are compared as numbers, so 1 and 01 clash. A missing order is missing-required-field. Give each capability in the domain its own whole-number `order`.
query:
SELECT severity, "check", record, message FROM (
  SELECT 'error' AS severity, 'capability-order' AS "check", nullif(c.id, '') AS record,
         'Capability ' || coalesce(nullif(c.id, ''), c.path) || ' has order "' || c.raw
         || '", which is not a whole number such as 1 or 2.' AS message
  FROM (
    SELECT r.path, r.id, trim(f.value) AS raw
    FROM records r JOIN fields f ON f.path = r.path AND f.name = 'order'
    WHERE r.kind = 'capability' AND trim(f.value) <> ''
  ) c
  WHERE NOT regexp_full_match(c.raw, '\d+')
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'error', 'capability-order', nullif(a.id, ''),
         'Capability ' || coalesce(nullif(a.id, ''), a.path) || ' has order ' || a.n || ' in domain ' || a.parent
         || ', the same as ' || string_agg(coalesce(nullif(b.id, ''), b.path), ', ' ORDER BY b.id, b.path)
         || '; each capability in a domain needs its own order.'
  FROM (
    SELECT r.path, r.id, r.parent, TRY_CAST(trim(f.value) AS HUGEINT) AS n
    FROM records r JOIN fields f ON f.path = r.path AND f.name = 'order'
    WHERE r.kind = 'capability' AND regexp_full_match(trim(f.value), '\d+')
  ) a
  JOIN (
    SELECT r.path, r.id, r.parent, TRY_CAST(trim(f.value) AS HUGEINT) AS n
    FROM records r JOIN fields f ON f.path = r.path AND f.name = 'order'
    WHERE r.kind = 'capability' AND regexp_full_match(trim(f.value), '\d+')
  ) b ON b.parent = a.parent AND b.n = a.n AND b.path <> a.path
  GROUP BY a.id, a.path, a.n, a.parent
)
ORDER BY record, message

name: component-file-missing
summary: A component whose file does not exist yet.
explanation: The design may name a file before it is written, so this is work to do, not breakage. Write the file, or fix the path (relative to the repo root).
query:
SELECT 'warning' AS severity, 'component-file-missing' AS "check", nullif(record, '') AS record,
       'Component ' || coalesce(nullif(record, ''), path) || ' names ' || file || ', which does not exist yet.' AS message
FROM file_facts
WHERE kind = 'component' AND NOT file_exists
ORDER BY path

name: component-outside-layer
summary: Once a domain has layers, each of its components sits in one of them.
explanation: This works as use cases sit in capabilities (29-use-case-outside-capability.sql). A domain with no layers may hold its components itself. Make one of the domain's layers the component's `parent`; its ID does not change.
query:
SELECT 'warning' AS severity, 'component-outside-layer' AS "check", c.id AS record,
       'Component ' || c.id || ' sits directly under domain ' || c.parent
       || ', which has layers; move it into the layer it belongs to.' AS message
FROM records c
JOIN records d ON d.id = c.parent AND d.kind = 'domain'
WHERE c.kind = 'component' AND c.id <> ''
  AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM records l WHERE l.kind = 'layer' AND l.parent = d.id)
ORDER BY record

name: component-satisfies-nothing
summary: A component that satisfies no obligation.
explanation: A component exists to design or implement something the product owes, so it links each obligation it serves with a `design` link such as `satisfies`. One with no such link has no purpose the spec can see: it is a leftover, or its purpose is unwritten. Shared infrastructure is no exception: link the requirements, domain rules or pattern rules it makes possible. A link to a record that does not exist does not count (it is only a dangling-link). Link what the component designs or implements with "satisfies", or remove it.
query:
SELECT 'warning' AS severity, 'component-satisfies-nothing' AS "check", c.id AS record,
       'Component ' || c.id || ' satisfies no obligation; link each requirement, domain rule or pattern rule it '
       || 'designs or implements with "satisfies" (for shared infrastructure, the ones it makes possible), '
       || 'or remove it.' AS message
FROM records c
WHERE c.kind = 'component' AND c.id <> ''
  AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM links l
    JOIN records t ON t.id = l.target
    JOIN relations ro ON ro.role = 'design' AND ro.relation = l.relation AND ro.source_kind = c.kind
                     AND ro.target_kind IN (t.kind, '*')
    WHERE l.path = c.path
  )
ORDER BY record

name: dangling-link
summary: Every link points at a record that exists.
explanation: A link whose target ID is no record is reported once for each source, relation and target. Fix the ID, or remove the link if its target was removed on purpose.
query:
SELECT DISTINCT 'error' AS severity, 'dangling-link' AS "check", nullif(l.source, '') AS record,
       coalesce(nullif(l.source, ''), l.path) || ' ' || l.relation || ' ' || l.target || ', which does not exist.' AS message
FROM links l
WHERE l.target NOT IN (SELECT id FROM records)
ORDER BY record, message

name: design-flow-deepens-nothing
summary: A technical flow that deepens no flow.
explanation: A technical flow says how the system carries out a flow (FORMAT.md section 21), so it names that flow with `deepens`. One that deepens nothing is design with no flow to carry out: the flow is missing, or the link is. A link to a flow that does not exist is only dangling-link. Link the flow it carries out with `deepens`, or write the flow first.
query:
SELECT 'warning' AS severity, 'design-flow-deepens-nothing' AS "check", d.id AS record,
       'Technical flow ' || d.id || ' deepens no flow; link the flow it carries out with "deepens".' AS message
FROM records d
WHERE d.kind = 'design_flow' AND d.id <> ''
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM links l WHERE l.path = d.path AND l.relation = 'deepens')
ORDER BY record

name: domain-named-for-technology
summary: A domain is named for a technology layer or delivery channel rather than a business capability.
explanation: A domain is a vertical slice of business capability (FORMAT.md section 18): it owns its records and rules, its views, its code and its tests, and technology is a layer inside its Design stage. A domain whose title or domain code (its ID after the product prefix, such as LEND in TL-LEND) names a technology splits one capability across several domains. The words are web app, frontend, front end, backend, back end, API, UI, server, database, DB, desktop, mobile, engine, infrastructure, infra and Electron, matched as whole words in any letter case, with or without a space or hyphen inside the two-word ones, and in the plural. Only the title and code are read, never the body, which may well say which technologies the domain uses. Name the domain for the capability it serves, and make the technology a layer in each domain's Design stage.
query:
SELECT 'warning' AS severity, 'domain-named-for-technology' AS "check", id AS record,
       'Domain ' || id || ' is named for a technology, not a business capability: '
       || CASE WHEN in_title <> '' THEN 'its title "' || trim(title) || '" says "' || in_title || '"' ELSE '' END
       || CASE WHEN in_title <> '' AND in_code <> '' THEN ' and ' ELSE '' END
       || CASE WHEN in_code <> '' THEN 'its code ' || code || ' says "' || in_code || '"' ELSE '' END
       || '; name the domain for the capability it serves, and make the technology a layer in each domain''s '
       || 'Design stage.' AS message
FROM (
  SELECT id, title, code,
         regexp_extract(lower(coalesce(title, '')), '(^|[^a-z])(' || words || ')([^a-z]|$)', 2) AS in_title,
         regexp_extract(lower(code), '(^|[^a-z])(' || words || ')([^a-z]|$)', 2) AS in_code
  FROM (
    -- Each domain's code is its ID after the product prefix.
    SELECT id, title,
           CASE WHEN parent IS NOT NULL AND starts_with(id, parent || '-') THEN substr(id, length(parent) + 2)
                ELSE id END AS code
    FROM records
    WHERE kind = 'domain' AND id <> ''
  ),
  (SELECT 'web[ -]?apps?|front[ -]?ends?|back[ -]?ends?|apis?|uis?|servers?|databases?|dbs?|desktops?|mobile'
          || '|engines?|infrastructure|infra|electron' AS words)
)
WHERE in_title <> '' OR in_code <> ''
ORDER BY record

name: domain-rule-involves
summary: A domain rule under its domain names the aggregates it ties together with `involves`; a rule under an aggregate or entity names none.
explanation: A domain rule sits on the aggregate, or the entity, it is about. One that holds across aggregates, such as two records saved together or a lifecycle rule for every record in the domain, sits under the domain (FORMAT.md section 16) and says with `involves` which aggregates it ties together. Such a rule is reported when it involves fewer than two aggregates: a rule about one aggregate belongs under that aggregate. It is also reported, once per link, for each aggregate it involves from another domain, since a rule across domains is a domain event's job: one domain raises the event and the other reacts to it. A rule under an aggregate or an entity that uses `involves` is reported too, since its place already says what it is about. Only links to aggregates are counted; a link to a record that does not exist, or that is not an aggregate, is reported by dangling-link or relation-not-allowed instead. A rule whose parent is missing or unknown is not judged. Name the aggregates, move a one-aggregate rule under its aggregate, or drop the link.
query:
SELECT 'warning' AS severity, 'domain-rule-involves' AS "check", nullif(f.id, '') AS record, f.message
FROM (
  WITH rules AS (
    -- Each domain rule with the kind of its parent; a duplicated parent ID counts once per kind it has.
    SELECT DISTINCT r.path, r.id, r.parent, r.domain, p.kind AS parent_kind
    FROM records r
    JOIN records p ON p.id = r.parent AND p.kind IN ('domain', 'aggregate', 'entity')
    WHERE r.kind = 'domain_rule'
  ),
  involved AS (
    -- Each aggregate a rule involves, with that aggregate's domain.
    SELECT DISTINCT l.path, l.target, t.domain AS target_domain
    FROM links l
    JOIN records t ON t.id = l.target AND t.kind = 'aggregate'
    WHERE l.relation = 'involves'
  )
  -- A rule under its domain that involves fewer than two aggregates.
  SELECT r.id,
         'Domain rule ' || coalesce(nullif(r.id, ''), r.path) || ' sits under the domain ' || r.parent || ' but involves '
         || CASE count(DISTINCT i.target) WHEN 0 THEN 'no aggregate; name with involves the two or more aggregates it '
                                                     || 'ties together, or move it under the aggregate it is about.'
            ELSE 'only ' || min(i.target) || '; a rule about one aggregate belongs under it, so move it under '
                 || min(i.target) || ', or name with involves every aggregate it ties together.' END AS message
  FROM rules r
  LEFT JOIN involved i ON i.path = r.path
  WHERE r.parent_kind = 'domain'
  GROUP BY r.path, r.id, r.parent
  HAVING count(DISTINCT i.target) < 2
  UNION ALL
  -- Each aggregate of another domain that a rule under its domain involves.
  SELECT r.id,
         'Domain rule ' || coalesce(nullif(r.id, ''), r.path) || ' involves ' || i.target || ', an aggregate of '
         || coalesce(i.target_domain, 'no domain') || ', not of its own domain ' || r.parent
         || '; a rule across domains is a domain event''s job, so have one domain raise an event and the other react to it.'
  FROM rules r
  JOIN involved i ON i.path = r.path
  WHERE r.parent_kind = 'domain' AND i.target_domain IS DISTINCT FROM r.domain
  UNION ALL
  -- A rule under an aggregate or an entity that uses involves at all.
  SELECT r.id,
         'Domain rule ' || coalesce(nullif(r.id, ''), r.path) || ' sits under the ' || r.parent_kind || ' ' || r.parent
         || ' and involves ' || string_agg(DISTINCT l.target, ', ' ORDER BY l.target)
         || '; its place already says what it is about, so drop involves, or move it under its domain if it holds '
         || 'across aggregates.'
  FROM rules r
  JOIN links l ON l.path = r.path AND l.relation = 'involves'
  WHERE r.parent_kind IN ('aggregate', 'entity')
  GROUP BY r.path, r.id, r.parent, r.parent_kind
) f
ORDER BY record, message

name: duplicate-id
summary: Every record ID is unique across the whole workspace.
explanation: Links, parents and coverage name records by ID, so two records with one ID make every reference to it ambiguous. Each record with the repeated ID is reported. Give all but one of them a new ID; IDs are never reused, so pick the next free number rather than an old one.
query:
SELECT 'error' AS severity, 'duplicate-id' AS "check", id AS record,
       'ID ' || id || ' is used by ' || count(*) || ' files: ' || string_agg(path, ', ' ORDER BY path) || '.' AS message
FROM records
WHERE id <> ''
GROUP BY id
HAVING count(*) > 1
ORDER BY id

name: entity-fields
summary: Each entity or event lists its fields in a Fields table.
explanation: An entity's table lists the fields it keeps and a domain event's the fields it carries. The table sits under a `## Fields` heading (FORMAT.md sections 16 and 17), with the columns Field, Meaning, Kind of value and Example, in any letter case, one row per field and each field name once. The engine reads the table into entity_tables and, when its columns are right, its rows into entity_fields. Field names are compared trimmed, without code span backticks, and in any letter case. A table with the wrong columns is reported for that alone. Add the heading and table, fix its columns, or merge the repeated field.
query:
SELECT 'error' AS severity, 'entity-fields' AS "check", nullif(t.record, '') AS record,
       CASE WHEN r.kind = 'domain_event' THEN 'Event' ELSE 'Entity' END || ' ' || coalesce(nullif(t.record, ''), t.path) || CASE
         WHEN NOT t.heading THEN ' has no ## Fields table; add a "## Fields" heading with a table of the columns '
                                 || w.wanted || ', one row per field.'
         WHEN t.columns IS NULL THEN ' has a ## Fields heading but no table under it; add a table of the columns '
                                     || w.wanted || ', one row per field.'
         ELSE '''s Fields table has the columns ' || t.columns || '; use the columns ' || w.wanted || ', in that order.'
       END AS message
FROM entity_tables t
LEFT JOIN records r ON r.path = t.path
CROSS JOIN (SELECT 'Field, Meaning, Kind of value and Example' AS wanted) w
WHERE NOT t.heading OR NOT t.columns_ok
UNION ALL
SELECT 'error', 'entity-fields', nullif(any_value(f.record), ''),
       any_value(CASE WHEN r.kind = 'domain_event' THEN 'Event' ELSE 'Entity' END) || ' ' || coalesce(nullif(any_value(f.record), ''), f.path)
       || '''s Fields table lists the field "' || arg_min(trim(f.field, ' `'), f.position) || '" ' || count(*)
       || ' times, in rows ' || string_agg(f.position::VARCHAR, ', ' ORDER BY f.position) || '; name each field once.'
FROM entity_fields f
LEFT JOIN records r ON r.path = f.path
WHERE trim(f.field, ' `') <> ''
GROUP BY f.path, lower(trim(f.field, ' `'))
HAVING count(*) > 1
UNION ALL
SELECT 'error', 'entity-fields', nullif(f.record, ''),
       CASE WHEN r.kind = 'domain_event' THEN 'Event' ELSE 'Entity' END || ' ' || coalesce(nullif(f.record, ''), f.path) || '''s Fields table has no field name in row '
       || f.position || '; name the field, or remove the row.'
FROM entity_fields f
LEFT JOIN records r ON r.path = f.path
WHERE trim(f.field, ' `') = ''
ORDER BY record, message

name: entity-role
summary: An entity's role is root or child.
explanation: `root` is the aggregate's root record and `child` one of its parts (FORMAT.md section 16), in any letter case. A missing or empty role is missing-required-field only. Fix the `role` value.
query:
SELECT 'error' AS severity, 'entity-role' AS "check", nullif(r.id, '') AS record,
       'Entity ' || coalesce(nullif(r.id, ''), r.path) || ' has role "' || trim(f.value)
       || '"; set role to root, for the aggregate''s root record, or child, for one of its parts.' AS message
FROM records r
JOIN fields f ON f.path = r.path AND f.name = 'role'
WHERE r.kind = 'entity' AND trim(f.value) <> '' AND lower(trim(f.value)) NOT IN ('root', 'child')
ORDER BY record, message

name: entity-unreferenced
summary: A child entity that its aggregate's root does not reach.
explanation: Each child entity is a part of its aggregate's root (FORMAT.md section 16), so a `has_one` or `has_many` reaches it from the root, directly or through other children of the same aggregate. Links that cross aggregates (has-crosses-aggregate) and `refers_to` links do not count. An aggregate with no root, or more than one, is aggregate-root only, so its children are not reported. Link the child from the root or from another child with `has_one` or `has_many`.
query:
SELECT 'warning' AS severity, 'entity-unreferenced' AS "check", e.id AS record,
       'Child entity ' || e.id || ' is not reached from ' || e.aggregate || '''s root ' || e.root
       || ' by has_one or has_many; link it from ' || e.root || ' or from the child it is a part of.' AS message
FROM (
  WITH RECURSIVE
    entities AS (
      SELECT e.id, e.parent AS aggregate, lower(trim(coalesce(f.value, ''))) AS role
      FROM records e
      LEFT JOIN fields f ON f.path = e.path AND f.name = 'role'
      WHERE e.kind = 'entity' AND e.id <> ''
    ),
    roots AS (
      SELECT aggregate, any_value(id) AS root FROM entities WHERE role = 'root' GROUP BY aggregate HAVING count(*) = 1
    ),
    parts AS (
      SELECT DISTINCT s.id AS source, t.id AS target
      FROM links l
      JOIN entities s ON s.id = l.source
      JOIN entities t ON t.id = l.target AND t.aggregate = s.aggregate
      WHERE l.relation IN ('has_one', 'has_many')
    ),
    reached (id) AS (
      SELECT root FROM roots
      UNION
      SELECT p.target FROM parts p JOIN reached r ON r.id = p.source
    )
  SELECT e.id, e.aggregate, r.root
  FROM entities e
  JOIN roots r ON r.aggregate = e.aggregate
  WHERE e.role = 'child' AND e.id NOT IN (SELECT id FROM reached)
) e
ORDER BY record

name: event-tense
summary: A domain event's title reads as something that happened, in the past tense.
explanation:
An event is named for what happened, such as Loan opened or Payment sent (FORMAT.md section 17). The check is a heuristic over the title's words, in any letter case and split at anything but a letter: the title passes when its last word, or any word after its first (the word after a one-word subject, as in Loan became overdue), is a past form. A past form is a word of four or more letters ending in "-ed", other than the few such words that are not verbs in the past (need, seed, feed, speed, breed, bleed, embed, proceed, exceed, succeed, hundred, naked, sacred, wicked), or one of the irregular past forms listed below. An empty title is missing-title only. The heuristic can miss a past form it does not know, so this is a warning. Name the event in the past tense, as what happened (Tool returned, not Return tool), or add the word to the list here if it is a past form the check does not know.

Irregular past forms: arose, arisen, ate, eaten, awoke, awoken, became, begun, began, bent, bound, bit, bitten, blew, blown, broke, broken, bred, brought, built, burnt, bought, caught, chose, chosen, came, cost, crept, cut, dealt, dug, did, done, drew, drawn, dreamt, drank, drunk, drove, driven, fell, fallen, fed, felt, fought, found, fled, flew, flown, forbade, forbidden, forgot, forgotten, forgave, forgiven, froze, frozen, got, gotten, gave, given, went, gone, grew, grown, hung, had, heard, hid, hidden, hit, held, hurt, kept, knew, known, laid, led, leant, learnt, left, lent, let, lit, lost, made, meant, met, mistook, mistaken, overdone, overran, overridden, overrode, overtaken, overtook, paid, put, quit, read, rebuilt, redone, remade, reran, rerun, reset, resent, resold, retook, retaken, rewound, rewrote, rewritten, rode, ridden, rang, rung, rose, risen, ran, run, said, saw, seen, sought, sold, sent, set, shook, shaken, shone, shot, showed, shown, shut, sang, sung, sank, sunk, sat, slept, slid, spoke, spoken, sped, spent, spun, split, spread, sprang, sprung, stood, stole, stolen, stuck, struck, swore, sworn, swept, swam, swum, swung, took, taken, taught, tore, torn, told, thought, threw, thrown, understood, undid, undone, upheld, upset, withdrew, withdrawn, withheld, woke, woken, wore, worn, won, wound, wrote, written.
query:
SELECT 'warning' AS severity, 'event-tense' AS "check", nullif(e.id, '') AS record,
       'Event ' || coalesce(nullif(e.id, ''), e.path) || ' is titled "' || trim(e.title)
       || '", which does not read as past tense; name it for what happened, such as "Loan opened" or "Tool '
       || 'returned".' AS message
FROM records e
WHERE e.kind = 'domain_event' AND regexp_matches(lower(coalesce(e.title, '')), '[a-z]')
  AND e.path NOT IN (
    -- Events with a past form as the title's last word, or as any word after its first.
    SELECT w.path
    FROM (
      SELECT path, unnest(words) AS word, unnest(generate_series(1, len(words))) AS position, len(words) AS count
      FROM (
        SELECT path, string_split(trim(regexp_replace(lower(title), '[^a-z]+', ' ', 'g')), ' ') AS words
        FROM records
        WHERE kind = 'domain_event'
      )
    ) w
    WHERE (w.position > 1 OR w.position = w.count)
      AND (list_contains(string_split(
      'arose arisen ate eaten awoke awoken became begun began bent bound bit bitten blew blown broke broken bred '
      || 'brought built burnt bought caught chose chosen came cost crept cut dealt dug did done drew drawn dreamt '
      || 'drank drunk drove driven fell fallen fed felt fought found fled flew flown forbade forbidden forgot '
      || 'forgotten forgave forgiven froze frozen got gotten gave given went gone grew grown hung had heard hid '
      || 'hidden hit held hurt kept knew known laid led leant learnt left lent let lit lost made meant met mistook '
      || 'mistaken overdone overran overridden overrode overtaken overtook paid put quit read rebuilt redone remade '
      || 'reran rerun reset resent resold retook retaken rewound rewrote rewritten rode ridden rang rung rose risen '
      || 'ran run said saw seen sought sold sent set shook shaken shone shot showed shown shut sang sung sank sunk '
      || 'sat slept slid spoke spoken sped spent spun split spread sprang sprung stood stole stolen stuck struck '
      || 'swore sworn swept swam swum swung took taken taught tore torn told thought threw thrown understood undid '
      || 'undone upheld upset withdrew withdrawn withheld woke woken wore worn won wound wrote written', ' '), w.word)
           OR (length(w.word) >= 4 AND w.word LIKE '%ed' AND NOT list_contains(string_split(
      'need seed feed speed breed bleed embed proceed exceed succeed hundred naked sacred wicked', ' '), w.word)))
  )
ORDER BY record, message

name: event-unheard
summary: A domain event that nothing reacts to.
explanation: An event is worth naming when something changes because it happened (FORMAT.md section 17): an aggregate, which may sit in another aggregate or domain, a use case that starts, or a component that handles it, each linking to the event with `reacts_to`. An event kept only for the record can be fine, so this is a warning. A `reacts_to` link from any record counts here; one from a kind the meta-model does not allow is relation-not-allowed. Add `reacts_to` to what changes, starts or runs when the event happens, or leave the event unheard on purpose.
query:
SELECT 'warning' AS severity, 'event-unheard' AS "check", e.id AS record,
       'Nothing reacts to event ' || e.id || ' (' || e.title || '). That can be fine for an event kept for the '
       || 'record; otherwise add reacts_to: [' || e.id || '] to the aggregate that changes, the use case that '
       || 'starts or the component that handles it when it happens.' AS message
FROM records e
WHERE e.kind = 'domain_event' AND e.id <> ''
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM links l WHERE l.relation = 'reacts_to' AND l.target = e.id)
ORDER BY record

name: flow-fulfills-differs-from-steps
summary: A flow with steps fulfills something none of its steps fulfills.
explanation: Once a flow has steps, what the flow fulfills is the union of what its steps fulfill, so each `fulfills` link belongs on the step that does it. A flow with steps may leave its own `fulfills` out: its steps' links are enough. Move the link onto the step that carries it out.
query:
SELECT DISTINCT 'warning' AS severity, 'flow-fulfills-differs-from-steps' AS "check", f.id AS record,
       'Flow ' || f.id || ' fulfills ' || l.target || ', but none of its steps does; move the link onto the step that carries it out.' AS message
FROM records f
JOIN links l ON l.path = f.path AND l.relation = 'fulfills'
WHERE f.kind = 'flow' AND f.id <> ''
  AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM records s WHERE s.kind = 'flow_step' AND s.parent = f.id)
  AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM records s JOIN links sl ON sl.path = s.path AND sl.relation = 'fulfills'
    WHERE s.kind = 'flow_step' AND s.parent = f.id AND sl.target = l.target
  )
ORDER BY record, message

name: flow-step-fulfills-outside-flow
summary: A flow step fulfills something its flow does not carry out.
query:
SELECT severity, "check", record, message FROM (
WITH carried AS (
  -- Each flow and the use cases it carries out.
  SELECT DISTINCT f.id AS flow, f.domain, c.target AS use_case
  FROM records f JOIN links c ON c.path = f.path AND c.relation = 'carries_out'
  WHERE f.kind = 'flow' AND f.id <> ''
),
core AS (
  -- 1. Requirements of the use cases the flow carries out.
  SELECT DISTINCT c.flow, r.id AS target
  FROM carried c JOIN records r ON r.kind = 'requirement' AND r.parent = c.use_case
  UNION
  -- 2. Domain rules those use cases apply.
  SELECT DISTINCT c.flow, a.target
  FROM carried c
  JOIN records u ON u.id = c.use_case AND u.kind = 'use_case'
  JOIN links a ON a.path = u.path AND a.relation = 'applies'
  UNION
  -- 3. Rules of the patterns those use cases follow...
  SELECT DISTINCT c.flow, pr.id
  FROM carried c
  JOIN records u ON u.id = c.use_case AND u.kind = 'use_case'
  JOIN links fo ON fo.path = u.path AND fo.relation = 'follows'
  JOIN records pr ON pr.kind = 'pattern_rule' AND pr.parent = fo.target
  UNION
  -- ...or that the flow's domain follows.
  SELECT DISTINCT c.flow, pr.id
  FROM (SELECT DISTINCT flow, domain FROM carried) c
  JOIN records d ON d.id = c.domain AND d.kind = 'domain'
  JOIN links fo ON fo.path = d.path AND fo.relation = 'follows'
  JOIN records pr ON pr.kind = 'pattern_rule' AND pr.parent = fo.target
),
inside AS (
  SELECT flow, target FROM core
  UNION
  -- 4. Interaction requirements that fulfill one of those...
  SELECT DISTINCT k.flow, ir.id
  FROM core k
  JOIN links x ON x.relation = 'fulfills' AND x.target = k.target
  JOIN records ir ON ir.path = x.path AND ir.kind = 'interaction_requirement'
  UNION
  -- ...or that sit under the flow itself.
  SELECT DISTINCT c.flow, ir.id
  FROM (SELECT DISTINCT flow FROM carried) c
  JOIN records ir ON ir.kind = 'interaction_requirement' AND ir.parent = c.flow
)
SELECT DISTINCT 'warning' AS severity, 'flow-step-fulfills-outside-flow' AS "check", s.id AS record,
       'Flow step ' || s.id || ' fulfills ' || l.target || ', which its flow ' || s.parent
       || ' does not carry out: it is not a requirement of a use case the flow carries out ('
       || (SELECT string_agg(DISTINCT c.use_case, ', ' ORDER BY c.use_case) FROM carried c WHERE c.flow = s.parent)
       || '), nor a domain rule one of them applies, nor a rule of a pattern one of them or the domain follows,'
       || ' nor an interaction requirement that fulfills any of these or sits under the flow.' AS message
FROM records s
JOIN links l ON l.path = s.path AND l.relation = 'fulfills'
WHERE s.kind = 'flow_step' AND s.id <> ''
  -- The step's flow carries out at least one use case.
  AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM carried c WHERE c.flow = s.parent)
  -- The target exists and is a kind a step may fulfill.
  AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM records t WHERE t.id = l.target
                                         AND t.kind IN ('requirement', 'domain_rule', 'interaction_requirement', 'pattern_rule'))
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM inside i WHERE i.flow = s.parent AND i.target = l.target)
)
ORDER BY record, message

name: has-crosses-aggregate
summary: A `has_one` or `has_many` link stays inside its aggregate.
explanation: These relations link an entity to its parts, and parts belong to their aggregate (FORMAT.md section 16), so both ends sit in the same aggregate. Only `refers_to` may cross aggregates and domains. A link to a record that does not exist, or that is not an entity, is reported by dangling-link or relation-not-allowed instead. When the target ID is duplicated, the link is reported only if no entity with that ID shares the source's aggregate. Use `refers_to`, or move the part into the aggregate.
query:
SELECT 'error' AS severity, 'has-crosses-aggregate' AS "check", nullif(x.source, '') AS record,
       'Entity ' || coalesce(nullif(x.source, ''), x.path) || ' ' || x.relation || ' ' || x.target
       || ', which sits in ' || string_agg(DISTINCT x.target_parent, ' or ' ORDER BY x.target_parent)
       || ', not in ' || x.source_parent || '; a part belongs to its aggregate, so use refers_to, or move '
       || x.target || ' into ' || x.source_parent || '.' AS message
FROM (
  SELECT l.path, l.source, l.relation, l.target, s.parent AS source_parent, t.parent AS target_parent
  FROM links l
  JOIN records s ON s.path = l.path AND s.kind = 'entity'
  JOIN records t ON t.id = l.target AND t.kind = 'entity'
  WHERE l.relation IN ('has_one', 'has_many')
) x
GROUP BY x.path, x.source, x.relation, x.target, x.source_parent
HAVING NOT bool_or(x.target_parent IS NOT DISTINCT FROM x.source_parent)
ORDER BY record, message

name: interaction-requirement-fulfills-nothing
summary: An interaction requirement names what it carries out.
explanation: An interaction requirement carries out a use case's requirement, a domain rule or a pattern rule at a view, endpoint or flow, so it links what it carries out with `fulfills`. Add the `fulfills` link.
query:
SELECT 'warning' AS severity, 'interaction-requirement-fulfills-nothing' AS "check", r.id AS record,
       'Interaction requirement ' || r.id || ' fulfills nothing; link the requirement or domain rule it carries out with "fulfills".' AS message
FROM records r
WHERE r.kind = 'interaction_requirement' AND r.id <> ''
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM links l WHERE l.path = r.path AND l.relation = 'fulfills')
ORDER BY record

name: layer-order
summary: A layer's order is a whole number that no other layer beside it has.
explanation: This works as for capabilities (28-capability-order.sql). Layers beside each other share a parent: the domain, or the layer that holds them as sub-layers. Layers in different domains, and sub-layers of different layers, may share an order. A missing order is missing-required-field. Orders are compared as numbers, so 1 and 01 clash. Give each layer beside the others its own whole-number `order`.
query:
SELECT severity, "check", record, message FROM (
  SELECT 'error' AS severity, 'layer-order' AS "check", nullif(c.id, '') AS record,
         'Layer ' || coalesce(nullif(c.id, ''), c.path) || ' has order "' || c.raw
         || '", which is not a whole number such as 1 or 2.' AS message
  FROM (
    SELECT r.path, r.id, trim(f.value) AS raw
    FROM records r JOIN fields f ON f.path = r.path AND f.name = 'order'
    WHERE r.kind = 'layer' AND trim(f.value) <> ''
  ) c
  WHERE NOT regexp_full_match(c.raw, '\d+')
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'error', 'layer-order', nullif(a.id, ''),
         'Layer ' || coalesce(nullif(a.id, ''), a.path) || ' has order ' || a.n
         || CASE WHEN a.parent_kind = 'layer' THEN ' in layer ' ELSE ' in domain ' END || a.parent
         || ', the same as ' || string_agg(coalesce(nullif(b.id, ''), b.path), ', ' ORDER BY b.id, b.path)
         || CASE WHEN a.parent_kind = 'layer' THEN '; each sub-layer of a layer needs its own order.'
                 ELSE '; each layer in a domain needs its own order.' END
  FROM (
    SELECT r.path, r.id, r.parent, TRY_CAST(trim(f.value) AS HUGEINT) AS n,
           (SELECT any_value(p.kind) FROM records p WHERE p.id = r.parent) AS parent_kind
    FROM records r JOIN fields f ON f.path = r.path AND f.name = 'order'
    WHERE r.kind = 'layer' AND regexp_full_match(trim(f.value), '\d+')
  ) a
  JOIN (
    SELECT r.path, r.id, r.parent, TRY_CAST(trim(f.value) AS HUGEINT) AS n
    FROM records r JOIN fields f ON f.path = r.path AND f.name = 'order'
    WHERE r.kind = 'layer' AND regexp_full_match(trim(f.value), '\d+')
  ) b ON b.parent = a.parent AND b.n = a.n AND b.path <> a.path
  GROUP BY a.id, a.path, a.n, a.parent, a.parent_kind
)
ORDER BY record, message

name: link-crosses-product
summary: A link stays inside its product.
explanation: Each product is a space of its own: its records link only to records of the same product, whatever the relation (`satisfies`, `involves`, `applies` and every other). A link from a record of one product to a record of another is reported once for each source, relation and target. A record that sits under no product, and a link to a record that does not exist, are reported by other checks instead. When the target ID is duplicated, the link is reported only if no record with that ID is in the source's product. Remove the link; to point a reader at the other product, name the ID in prose, where it is a plain citation.
query:
SELECT 'error' AS severity, 'link-crosses-product' AS "check", x.source AS record,
       x.source || ' ' || x.relation || ' ' || x.target || ', a record of '
       || string_agg(DISTINCT x.target_product, ' or ' ORDER BY x.target_product) || ', not of its own product '
       || x.source_product || '; a link stays inside its product, so remove it, or name ' || x.target
       || ' in prose, where it is a plain citation.' AS message
FROM (
  SELECT l.source, l.relation, l.target, s.product AS source_product, t.product AS target_product
  FROM links l
  JOIN records s ON s.path = l.path AND s.id = l.source AND s.product IS NOT NULL
  JOIN records t ON t.id = l.target AND t.product IS NOT NULL
  WHERE l.source <> ''
) x
GROUP BY x.source, x.relation, x.target, x.source_product
HAVING NOT bool_or(x.target_product = x.source_product)
ORDER BY record, message

name: lone-child
summary: A capability, a layer or a group with exactly one child, of any kind.
explanation: A level that holds one record groups nothing. Only its own children are counted, not theirs, and one with no children is not reported. A group (the `group` of requirements, interaction requirements, pattern rules and standard rules, FORMAT.md section 22) is counted among its parent's children of one kind, compared trimmed and in any letter case, and reported on that parent. Merge it into a neighbor, or give it more.
query:
SELECT 'warning' AS severity, 'lone-child' AS "check", g.id AS record,
       upper(left(g.kind, 1)) || substr(g.kind, 2) || ' ' || g.id || ' has only one child, '
       || coalesce(nullif(g.child, ''), g.child_path)
       || '; merge it into a neighboring ' || g.kind || ', or give it more.' AS message
FROM (
  SELECT r.id, any_value(r.kind) AS kind, count(DISTINCT c.path) AS n,
         any_value(c.id) AS child, any_value(c.path) AS child_path
  FROM records r
  JOIN records c ON c.parent = r.id
  WHERE r.kind IN ('capability', 'layer') AND r.id <> ''
  GROUP BY r.id
) g
WHERE g.n = 1
UNION ALL
SELECT 'warning', 'lone-child', m.parent,
       upper(left(p.kind, 1)) || replace(substr(p.kind, 2), '_', ' ') || ' ' || m.parent || '''s group "' || m.label
       || '" has only one ' || replace(m.kind, '_', ' ') || ', ' || coalesce(nullif(m.child, ''), m.child_path)
       || '; merge it into a neighboring group, or give it more.'
FROM (
  SELECT r.parent, r.kind, lower(trim(g.value)) AS bucket, min(trim(g.value)) AS label, count(DISTINCT r.path) AS n,
         any_value(r.id) AS child, any_value(r.path) AS child_path
  FROM records r
  JOIN fields g ON g.path = r.path AND g.name = 'group' AND trim(g.value) <> ''
  WHERE r.kind IN ('requirement', 'interaction_requirement', 'pattern_rule', 'standard_rule') AND coalesce(r.parent, '') <> ''
  GROUP BY r.parent, r.kind, bucket
) m
JOIN (SELECT id, any_value(kind) AS kind FROM records WHERE id <> '' GROUP BY id) p ON p.id = m.parent
WHERE m.n = 1
ORDER BY record, message

name: manual-test-file-silent
summary: A manual test whose `run_by` file exists but never mentions it.
explanation: Nothing ties the file to the test: it names neither the test's ID, nor any ID the test proves (each target of a relation whose role is `proof`), nor the test's `key` when it has one. Manual tests are not held to the automated rules (test-file-missing-id, proof-not-in-file), so a silent file is a warning: the steps a person follows should say which test they carry out. A test with a `key_file` is judged by that file instead. A missing file is test-file-missing instead. Name the test in the file, or point `run_by` at the file that carries it out.
query:
SELECT 'warning' AS severity, 'manual-test-file-silent' AS "check", nullif(f.record, '') AS record,
       'Manual test ' || coalesce(nullif(f.record, ''), f.path)
       || CASE WHEN f.key_file IS NOT NULL THEN ' names the key file ' || f.key_file ELSE ' is run by ' || f.file END
       || ', but that file names neither '
       || coalesce(nullif(f.record, ''), 'the test''s ID') || ' nor any ID it proves'
       || coalesce(' nor its key "' || k.key || '"', '')
       || '; name the test in the file, or point run_by at the file that carries it out.' AS message
FROM file_facts f
LEFT JOIN (SELECT path, max(trim(value)) AS key FROM fields WHERE name = 'key' AND trim(value) <> '' GROUP BY path) k
       ON k.path = f.path
WHERE f.kind = 'test' AND f.file_exists AND NOT coalesce(f.contains_id, false) AND f.key_file_exists IS NOT false
  AND coalesce((SELECT max(lower(trim(s.value))) FROM fields s WHERE s.path = f.path AND s.name = 'state'), '') = 'manual'
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM file_mentions m WHERE m.path = f.path AND f.record <> '' AND m.mentioned = f.record)
  AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM links l
    JOIN records t ON t.id = l.target
    JOIN relations rr ON rr.relation = l.relation AND rr.role = 'proof' AND rr.source_kind = f.kind
                     AND rr.target_kind IN (t.kind, '*')
    JOIN file_mentions m ON m.path = f.path AND m.mentioned = l.target
    WHERE l.path = f.path
  )
ORDER BY f.path

name: meta-bad-required-field
summary: Each kind's required fields are valid field names.
explanation: A field name is lower-case letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter, and not one of the fields every record has (`id`, `kind`, `title`, `parent`, `links`). Rename the field in `kinds.csv`.
query:
SELECT DISTINCT 'error' AS severity, 'meta-bad-required-field' AS "check", NULL AS record,
       'Kind "' || kind || '" requires field "' || name || '", which is not a valid field name'
       || CASE WHEN name IN ('id', 'kind', 'title', 'parent', 'links') THEN ': every record already has it.'
               ELSE ': use lower-case letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter.' END AS message
FROM (SELECT kind, unnest(required_fields) AS name FROM kinds)
WHERE NOT regexp_full_match(name, '[a-z][a-z0-9_]*')
   OR name IN ('id', 'kind', 'title', 'parent', 'links')
ORDER BY message

name: meta-duplicate-kind
summary: Each meta-model folder defines a kind at most once.
explanation: A row in a later folder (a product's extension) for a kind already defined widens that kind; it is not a duplicate. Two rows for one kind in the same `kinds.csv` are reported, naming the file. Merge them into one row.
query:
SELECT 'error' AS severity, 'meta-duplicate-kind' AS "check", NULL AS record,
       folder || ' defines kind "' || kind || '" ' || count(*) || ' times; each kind must be defined once in a folder.' AS message
FROM meta_kind_rows
WHERE kind IS NOT NULL AND kind <> ''
GROUP BY folder, kind
HAVING count(*) > 1
ORDER BY folder, kind

name: meta-duplicate-relation
summary: Each meta-model folder lists a relation rule at most once.
explanation: A relation rule is a relation, a source kind and a target kind. A row in a later folder (a product's extension) for a rule already listed restates or rewords that rule; it is not a duplicate. Two rows for one rule in the same `relations.csv` are reported, naming the file. Merge them into one row.
query:
SELECT 'error' AS severity, 'meta-duplicate-relation' AS "check", NULL AS record,
       folder || ' lists relation rule "' || relation || '" from ' || source_kind || ' to ' || target_kind || ' '
       || count(*) || ' times; each rule must be listed once in a folder.' AS message
FROM meta_relation_rows
WHERE relation <> '' AND source_kind <> '' AND target_kind <> ''
GROUP BY folder, relation, source_kind, target_kind
HAVING count(*) > 1
ORDER BY folder, relation, source_kind, target_kind

name: meta-unknown-parent-kind
summary: Every kind named in a kind's `parent_kinds` is a kind the meta-model defines.
explanation: A misspelled parent kind allows no parent at all. Fix the name in `kinds.csv`, or define the kind.
query:
SELECT DISTINCT 'error' AS severity, 'meta-unknown-parent-kind' AS "check", NULL AS record,
       'Kind "' || p.kind || '" names parent kind "' || p.parent_kind || '", which the meta-model does not define.' AS message
FROM (SELECT kind, unnest(parent_kinds) AS parent_kind FROM kinds) p
WHERE p.parent_kind NOT IN (SELECT kind FROM kinds WHERE kind IS NOT NULL)
ORDER BY message

name: meta-unknown-relation-kind
summary: Every source and target kind of a relation rule is a kind the meta-model defines.
explanation: The `*` target, meaning any kind, is allowed. A misspelled kind makes the rule allow nothing. Fix the name in `relations.csv`, or define the kind.
query:
SELECT DISTINCT 'error' AS severity, 'meta-unknown-relation-kind' AS "check", NULL AS record,
       'Relation rule "' || coalesce(r.relation, '') || '" from ' || coalesce(r.source_kind, '(none)') || ' to '
       || coalesce(r.target_kind, '(none)') || ' names ' || s.side || ' kind "' || coalesce(s.name, '') || '", which the meta-model does not define.' AS message
FROM relations r,
     LATERAL (VALUES ('source', r.source_kind), ('target', r.target_kind)) AS s(side, name)
WHERE NOT (s.side = 'target' AND s.name = '*')
  AND (s.name IS NULL OR s.name NOT IN (SELECT kind FROM kinds WHERE kind IS NOT NULL))
ORDER BY message

name: missing-parent
summary: Every record except a product names its parent.
explanation: A record belongs to the record named in `parent`, which places it in its product and domain. Add the `parent` field, naming a record of one of the kind's allowed parent kinds.
query:
SELECT 'error' AS severity, 'missing-parent' AS "check", nullif(r.id, '') AS record,
       coalesce(nullif(r.id, ''), r.path) || ' (' || r.kind || ') has no parent; every ' || r.kind || ' must name one.' AS message
FROM records r
WHERE r.parent IS NULL
  AND r.kind <> 'product'
  AND r.kind IN (SELECT kind FROM kinds)
ORDER BY r.path

name: missing-required-field
summary: A record has every field its kind requires, with a non-empty value.
explanation: Each kind lists its required fields in `required_fields` (see the kind's reference), such as a use case's `actor` or a component's `file`. Add the missing field to the record's header with a value.
query:
SELECT 'error' AS severity, 'missing-required-field' AS "check", nullif(r.id, '') AS record,
       coalesce(nullif(r.id, ''), r.path) || ' (' || r.kind || ') has no "' || req.name || '" field, which every ' || r.kind || ' must have.' AS message
FROM records r
JOIN (SELECT kind, unnest(required_fields) AS name FROM kinds) req ON req.kind = r.kind
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM fields f WHERE f.path = r.path AND f.name = req.name AND trim(f.value) <> ''
)
ORDER BY r.path, req.name

name: missing-title
summary: Every record has a title.
explanation: A title is the short name every page and list shows. For a rule or requirement, it is the rule in a few words. Add a `title` field to the record's header.
query:
SELECT 'error' AS severity, 'missing-title' AS "check", nullif(id, '') AS record,
       coalesce(nullif(id, ''), path) || ' has no title.' AS message
FROM records
WHERE trim(title) = ''
ORDER BY path

name: obligation-outside-domain
summary: An obligation that sits in no domain.
explanation: It counts in no domain's coverage, so it is reported rather than silently dropped. A pattern rule under a pattern is the exception: each domain that follows the pattern owes it (pattern-not-followed reports a pattern nobody follows). Move the record under a domain, or fix its parent chain.
query:
SELECT DISTINCT 'warning' AS severity, 'obligation-outside-domain' AS "check", nullif(r.id, '') AS record,
       upper(left(r.kind, 1)) || replace(substr(r.kind, 2), '_', ' ') || ' ' || coalesce(nullif(r.id, ''), r.path)
       || ' sits in no domain, so no domain''s coverage counts it; move it under a domain.' AS message
FROM records r
WHERE r.domain IS NULL
  AND r.kind IN (SELECT kind FROM kinds WHERE obligation)
  AND NOT (r.kind = 'pattern_rule' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM records p WHERE p.id = r.parent AND p.kind = 'pattern'))
ORDER BY record, message

name: parent-kind-not-allowed
summary: A record's parent is of one of the kinds its kind allows as a parent.
explanation: Each kind lists its allowed parent kinds in `parent_kinds` (see the kind's reference). Products are covered by product-has-parent instead, and an unknown parent is unknown-parent only. When the parent ID is duplicated (duplicate-id), the record is reported only if no record with that ID could be its parent. Move the record under a parent of an allowed kind, or widen the kind's `parent_kinds` in the product's extension.
query:
SELECT 'error' AS severity, 'parent-kind-not-allowed' AS "check", nullif(x.id, '') AS record,
       coalesce(nullif(x.id, ''), x.path) || ' (' || x.kind || ') sits under ' || x.parent || ' ('
       || string_agg(DISTINCT x.parent_kind, ' or ' ORDER BY x.parent_kind)
       || '), but a ' || x.kind || ' must sit under: ' || array_to_string(any_value(x.parent_kinds), ', ') || '.' AS message
FROM (
  SELECT r.path, r.id, r.kind, r.parent, p.kind AS parent_kind, k.parent_kinds,
         list_contains(k.parent_kinds, p.kind) AS allowed
  FROM records r
  JOIN kinds k ON k.kind = r.kind
  JOIN records p ON p.id = r.parent
  WHERE r.kind <> 'product'
) x
GROUP BY x.path, x.id, x.kind, x.parent
HAVING NOT bool_or(x.allowed)
ORDER BY record, message

name: pattern-not-followed
summary: A pattern that no use case and no domain follows.
explanation: No domain owes its rules, so they count in no domain's coverage. Link the use cases or domains that apply it with `follows`, or remove the pattern if nothing needs it.
query:
SELECT 'warning' AS severity, 'pattern-not-followed' AS "check", p.id AS record,
       'No use case or domain follows pattern ' || p.id || ', so '
       || CASE (SELECT count(DISTINCT r.id) FROM records r WHERE r.kind = 'pattern_rule' AND r.parent = p.id AND r.id <> '')
            WHEN 0 THEN 'it is not used anywhere.'
            WHEN 1 THEN 'its 1 rule is not counted in any domain''s coverage.'
            ELSE 'its ' || (SELECT count(DISTINCT r.id) FROM records r WHERE r.kind = 'pattern_rule' AND r.parent = p.id AND r.id <> '')
                 || ' rules are not counted in any domain''s coverage.'
          END AS message
FROM (SELECT DISTINCT id FROM records WHERE kind = 'pattern' AND id <> '') p
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM links l JOIN records u ON u.id = l.source AND u.path = l.path
  WHERE l.relation = 'follows' AND l.target = p.id AND u.kind IN ('use_case', 'domain')
)
ORDER BY record

name: pattern-rule-setting-unknown
summary: A pattern rule's `setting` is one of the settings its pattern lists.
explanation: A pattern rule that depends on a setting names it in `setting`. A rule whose parent is not a pattern is reported by the parent checks instead. Fix the name, add the setting to the pattern, or remove the field if the rule depends on no setting.
query:
SELECT DISTINCT 'error' AS severity, 'pattern-rule-setting-unknown' AS "check", nullif(r.id, '') AS record,
       'Pattern rule ' || coalesce(nullif(r.id, ''), r.path) || ' depends on the setting "' || trim(st.value)
       || '", which pattern ' || p.id || ' does not list; '
       || CASE WHEN trim(coalesce(ps.value, '')) = '' THEN 'it has no settings.' ELSE 'its settings are: ' || trim(ps.value) || '.' END AS message
FROM records r
JOIN fields st ON st.path = r.path AND st.name = 'setting' AND trim(st.value) <> ''
JOIN records p ON p.id = r.parent AND p.kind = 'pattern'
LEFT JOIN fields ps ON ps.path = p.path AND ps.name = 'settings'
WHERE r.kind = 'pattern_rule'
  AND NOT list_contains(string_split_regex(trim(coalesce(ps.value, '')), '\s+'), trim(st.value))
ORDER BY record, message

name: pattern-setting-clash
summary: A use case follows two patterns that share a setting name.
explanation: The use case has one field for both settings, so the two cannot be given different values. Rename the setting in one of the patterns, and its field in the use cases that follow it.
query:
SELECT 'warning' AS severity, 'pattern-setting-clash' AS "check", x.use_case AS record,
       'Use case ' || x.use_case || ' follows patterns ' || string_agg(x.pattern, ' and ' ORDER BY x.pattern)
       || ', which share the setting "' || x.name || '"; its one "' || x.name || '" field answers both.' AS message
FROM (
  SELECT DISTINCT u.id AS use_case, s.pattern, s.name
  FROM records u
  JOIN links l ON l.path = u.path AND l.relation = 'follows'
  JOIN (
    SELECT DISTINCT p.id AS pattern, t.name
    FROM records p
    JOIN fields f ON f.path = p.path AND f.name = 'settings'
    CROSS JOIN unnest(string_split_regex(trim(f.value), '\s+')) AS t(name)
    WHERE p.kind = 'pattern' AND p.id <> '' AND t.name <> ''
  ) s ON s.pattern = l.target
  WHERE u.kind = 'use_case' AND u.id <> ''
) x
GROUP BY x.use_case, x.name
HAVING count(*) > 1
ORDER BY record, message

name: pattern-setting-missing
summary: A use case that follows a pattern gives each of the pattern's settings.
explanation: Each setting is a header field named exactly as the pattern lists it: a value, or "Not applicable:" (any letter case) and a reason. Setting names that are not valid field names are reported by bad-pattern-settings instead. Only a pattern with settings asks for them: a pattern with no `settings` field, or an empty one, asks nothing of the use cases that follow it. A domain that follows a pattern gives no settings. Add the missing field to the use case, or its reason for Not applicable.
query:
SELECT 'error' AS severity, 'pattern-setting-missing' AS "check", x.use_case AS record,
       CASE WHEN coalesce(x.value, '') = ''
            THEN 'Use case ' || x.use_case || ' follows pattern ' || x.pattern || ' but has no "' || x.name
                 || '" field; give it a value, or "Not applicable:" and a reason.'
            ELSE 'Use case ' || x.use_case || ' says pattern ' || x.pattern || '''s "' || x.name
                 || '" setting is not applicable but gives no reason after "Not applicable:".'
       END AS message
FROM (
  SELECT DISTINCT u.id AS use_case, s.pattern, s.name,
         (SELECT trim(any_value(f.value)) FROM fields f WHERE f.path = u.path AND f.name = s.name) AS value
  FROM records u
  JOIN links l ON l.path = u.path AND l.relation = 'follows'
  JOIN (
    SELECT DISTINCT p.id AS pattern, t.name
    FROM records p
    JOIN fields f ON f.path = p.path AND f.name = 'settings'
    CROSS JOIN unnest(string_split_regex(trim(f.value), '\s+')) AS t(name)
    WHERE p.kind = 'pattern' AND p.id <> '' AND t.name <> ''
      AND regexp_full_match(t.name, '[a-z][a-z0-9_]*') AND t.name NOT IN ('id', 'kind', 'title', 'parent', 'links')
  ) s ON s.pattern = l.target
  WHERE u.kind = 'use_case' AND u.id <> ''
) x
WHERE coalesce(x.value, '') = ''
   OR regexp_full_match(x.value, '(?i)not\s+applicable\s*:\s*')
ORDER BY record, message

name: product-has-parent
summary: A product is a root record and has no parent.
explanation: Every other record sits under a product, so a product itself sits under nothing. Remove the product's `parent` field.
query:
SELECT 'error' AS severity, 'product-has-parent' AS "check", nullif(id, '') AS record,
       coalesce(nullif(id, ''), path) || ' is a product, so it must not have a parent, but names ' || parent || '.' AS message
FROM records
WHERE kind = 'product' AND parent IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY path

name: proof-counts-nowhere
summary: A test whose proofs count in no domain's coverage.
explanation: A test's proof of a target counts, as in lathe/src/coverage.ts, when the target is an obligation in a domain, or a pattern rule owed by the domain the test sits in (the owed_pattern_rules table: a domain owes a pattern rule when it follows the pattern itself, or when one of its use cases does, unless the rule is Not applicable or waived there). A test is reported when it has at least one `proof` link to a record that exists and none of its proofs counts; the message says why for each target. A target that does not exist is only a dangling-link. The test's state does not matter: a planned test that will prove nothing counted is reported too. Point the test at an obligation that counts, or move it into the domain that owes the rule.
query:
SELECT severity, "check", record, message FROM (
WITH follows AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT l.target AS pattern
  FROM records u JOIN links l ON l.path = u.path AND l.relation = 'follows'
  WHERE u.kind IN ('use_case', 'domain') AND u.id <> ''
),
claims AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT s.path, s.id AS test, s.domain AS test_domain, t.id AS target, t.kind AS target_kind,
    t.domain AS target_domain, t.parent AS target_parent,
    t.kind IN (SELECT kind FROM kinds WHERE obligation) AS obligation,
    t.kind = 'pattern_rule' AND t.domain IS NULL AS shared
  FROM links l
  JOIN records s ON s.id = l.source AND s.path = l.path
  JOIN records t ON t.id = l.target
  JOIN relations ro ON ro.role = 'proof' AND ro.relation = l.relation AND ro.source_kind = s.kind
                   AND ro.target_kind IN (t.kind, '*')
  WHERE s.kind = 'test'
),
judged AS (
  SELECT c.*,
    c.obligation AND CASE WHEN c.shared
                          THEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM owed_pattern_rules o WHERE o.id = c.target AND o.domain = c.test_domain)
                          ELSE c.target_domain IS NOT NULL END AS counts,
    (SELECT string_agg(DISTINCT o.domain, ', ' ORDER BY o.domain) FROM owed_pattern_rules o WHERE o.id = c.target) AS owers
  FROM claims c
),
explained AS (
  SELECT path, test, counts, target || CASE
      WHEN NOT obligation THEN ' is not an obligation'
      WHEN NOT shared THEN ' sits in no domain'
      WHEN owers IS NOT NULL THEN ' is owed only by ' || owers || ', not by '
           || coalesce(test_domain || ', where the test sits', 'the test, which sits in no domain')
      WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM follows f WHERE f.pattern = target_parent)
           THEN ' is owed by no domain: wherever ' || target_parent
                || ' is followed, its setting is Not applicable or no follower meets its applies_when'
      ELSE ' is owed by no domain: no use case follows its pattern ' || coalesce(target_parent, '')
    END AS reason
  FROM judged
),
reasons AS (
  SELECT path, test, bool_or(counts) AS any_counts, string_agg(DISTINCT reason, '; ' ORDER BY reason) AS why
  FROM explained
  GROUP BY path, test
)
SELECT 'warning' AS severity, 'proof-counts-nowhere' AS "check", nullif(test, '') AS record,
       'Test ' || coalesce(nullif(test, ''), path) || '''s proof counts in no domain''s coverage: ' || why
       || '. Prove what the test''s domain owes, or move the test into a domain that owes what it proves.' AS message
FROM reasons
WHERE NOT any_counts
)
ORDER BY record, message

name: proof-not-in-file
summary: An automated test's file names every ID the test proves, unless it names the test's own ID.
explanation: Each target of a relation whose role is `proof` must appear in the file, as a whole ID, when the file does not name the test's own ID. Each proved ID the file leaves out is one error. A test whose file names its own ID vouches for all its claims; a test with a `key` is checked by test-file-missing-id instead. A test with a `key_file` is judged by that file instead of `run_by`; a key file that is missing or outside the root is test-file-missing only. A `supports` link is not a proof claim, so its target need not appear. Manual and planned tests are not checked here. Name the ID in the test's name in the file, name the test's own ID there, or remove the claim.
query:
SELECT 'error' AS severity, 'proof-not-in-file' AS "check", nullif(record, '') AS record,
       'Test ' || coalesce(nullif(record, ''), path) || ' proves ' || target || ', but its '
       || CASE WHEN key_file IS NOT NULL THEN 'key file ' || key_file ELSE 'file ' || file END
       || ' names neither ' || coalesce(nullif(record, ''), 'the test''s ID') || ' nor ' || target
       || '; name the test''s ID, or every ID it proves, in that file.' AS message
FROM (
  SELECT DISTINCT f.path, f.record, f.file, f.key_file, l.target
  FROM file_facts f
  JOIN links l ON l.path = f.path
  JOIN records t ON t.id = l.target
  JOIN relations rr ON rr.relation = l.relation AND rr.role = 'proof' AND rr.source_kind = f.kind
                   AND (rr.target_kind = t.kind OR rr.target_kind = '*')
  WHERE f.kind = 'test' AND f.file_exists AND NOT f.contains_id AND f.key_file_exists IS NOT false
    AND coalesce((SELECT max(lower(trim(s.value))) FROM fields s WHERE s.path = f.path AND s.name = 'state'), '')
        NOT IN ('manual', 'planned')
    AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM fields k WHERE k.path = f.path AND k.name = 'key' AND trim(k.value) <> '')
    AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM file_mentions m WHERE m.path = f.path AND m.mentioned = l.target)
)
ORDER BY path, target

name: proof-still-owed
summary: An obligation that is already proved, but that a planned test is also meant to prove.
explanation:
Coverage counts these in `planned_any` but not in `planned`; this check names each one, with the planned test that still owes its proof, so the list behind `planned_any` is never only a count. An obligation not yet proved whose test is only planned is reported by unproved instead.

Proof is judged as in lathe/src/coverage.ts: an obligation in a domain is owed by that domain and any test may prove it; a pattern rule is owed by the domains the owed_pattern_rules table names (unless Not applicable or waived there), and only tests in that domain prove it there or owe it there. An automated test's proof counts only when its file backs it. Write the planned test, or drop its claim if the proof it owes is already made.
query:
SELECT severity, "check", record, message FROM (
WITH states AS (
  SELECT path, record, lower(trim(any_value(value))) AS state FROM fields WHERE name = 'state' GROUP BY path, record
),
proof_links AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT l.target, t.kind AS target_kind, s.id AS source, s.domain AS source_domain,
    coalesce(nullif(st.state, ''), 'automated') AS state,
    CASE WHEN s.kind <> 'test' OR coalesce(nullif(st.state, ''), 'automated') <> 'automated' THEN true
         ELSE coalesce((SELECT bool_or(f.contains_id) FROM file_facts f WHERE f.path = s.path), false)
              OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM file_mentions m WHERE m.path = s.path AND m.mentioned = l.target)
    END AS backed
  FROM links l
  JOIN records s ON s.id = l.source AND s.path = l.path
  JOIN records t ON t.id = l.target
  JOIN relations ro ON ro.role = 'proof' AND ro.relation = l.relation AND ro.source_kind = s.kind
                   AND ro.target_kind IN (t.kind, '*')
  LEFT JOIN states st ON st.path = s.path AND st.record = s.id
),
owed AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT r.domain, r.id, r.kind, false AS per_domain
  FROM records r
  WHERE r.domain IS NOT NULL AND r.id <> '' AND r.kind IN (SELECT kind FROM kinds WHERE obligation)
  UNION
  SELECT domain, id, kind, true AS per_domain FROM owed_pattern_rules
)
SELECT DISTINCT 'warning' AS severity, 'proof-still-owed' AS "check", o.id AS record,
       upper(left(o.kind, 1)) || replace(substr(o.kind, 2), '_', ' ') || ' ' || o.id || ' is proved'
       || CASE WHEN o.per_domain THEN ' in ' || o.domain ELSE '' END
       || ', but planned test ' || p.source || CASE WHEN o.per_domain THEN ' there' ELSE '' END
       || ' still owes a proof of it; write that test, or drop its proves link to ' || o.id || '.' AS message
FROM owed o
JOIN proof_links p ON p.target = o.id AND p.target_kind = o.kind AND p.state = 'planned' AND p.source <> ''
                  AND (NOT o.per_domain OR p.source_domain = o.domain)
WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM proof_links x WHERE x.target = o.id AND x.target_kind = o.kind
                                            AND x.state IN ('automated', 'manual') AND x.backed
                                            AND (NOT o.per_domain OR x.source_domain = o.domain))
)
ORDER BY record, message

name: raised-by-outside-aggregate
summary: A domain event's `raised_by` names an entity of the event's own aggregate.
explanation: An event is raised by its aggregate (FORMAT.md section 17), so the entity whose change raises it is one of that aggregate's entities. What another aggregate does about the event is said by its `reacts_to`. An event with no `raised_by` is not reported. A link to a record that does not exist, or that is not an entity, is reported by dangling-link or relation-not-allowed instead. When the target ID is duplicated, the link is reported only if no entity with that ID shares the event's aggregate. Point `raised_by` at an entity of the event's aggregate, or move the event under the aggregate that raises it.
query:
SELECT 'error' AS severity, 'raised-by-outside-aggregate' AS "check", nullif(x.source, '') AS record,
       'Event ' || coalesce(nullif(x.source, ''), x.path) || ' is raised_by ' || x.target || ', which sits in '
       || string_agg(DISTINCT x.target_parent, ' or ' ORDER BY x.target_parent) || ', not in the event''s aggregate '
       || x.source_parent || '; point raised_by at an entity of ' || x.source_parent
       || ', or move the event under the aggregate that raises it.' AS message
FROM (
  SELECT l.path, l.source, l.target, s.parent AS source_parent, t.parent AS target_parent
  FROM links l
  JOIN records s ON s.path = l.path AND s.kind = 'domain_event'
  JOIN records t ON t.id = l.target AND t.kind = 'entity'
  WHERE l.relation = 'raised_by'
) x
GROUP BY x.path, x.source, x.target, x.source_parent
HAVING NOT bool_or(x.target_parent IS NOT DISTINCT FROM x.source_parent)
ORDER BY record, message

name: relation-not-allowed
summary: A known relation is allowed from the source record's kind to the target record's kind.
explanation: Each row of `relations.csv` allows one relation from one source kind to one target kind (`*` allows any target kind). When the target ID is duplicated (duplicate-id), the link is reported only if no record with that ID could be its target, so one duplicate does not turn every link to it into an error. Link to a record of an allowed kind, use the relation meant for this pair, or allow the pair in the product's extension.
query:
SELECT 'error' AS severity, 'relation-not-allowed' AS "check", nullif(x.source, '') AS record,
       coalesce(nullif(x.source, ''), x.path) || ' (' || x.source_kind || ') ' || x.relation || ' ' || x.target || ' ('
       || string_agg(DISTINCT x.target_kind, ' or ' ORDER BY x.target_kind) || '), but "' || x.relation
       || '" is not allowed from ' || x.source_kind || ' to '
       || string_agg(DISTINCT x.target_kind, ' or ' ORDER BY x.target_kind) || '.' AS message
FROM (
  SELECT l.path, l.source, l.relation, l.target, s.kind AS source_kind, t.kind AS target_kind,
         EXISTS (
           SELECT 1 FROM relations rr
           WHERE rr.relation = l.relation AND rr.source_kind = s.kind AND (rr.target_kind = t.kind OR rr.target_kind = '*')
         ) AS allowed
  FROM links l
  JOIN records s ON s.path = l.path
  JOIN records t ON t.id = l.target
  WHERE l.relation IN (SELECT relation FROM relations)
    AND s.kind IN (SELECT kind FROM kinds)
) x
GROUP BY x.path, x.source, x.relation, x.target, x.source_kind
HAVING NOT bool_or(x.allowed)
ORDER BY record, message

name: relation-unlabeled
summary: Every relation rule says in plain words what its link means, read from either end.
explanation: Each row of `relations.csv`, Lathe's or an extension's, carries a `forward_label`, the link read from the source ("Satisfies"), and a `reverse_label`, the link read from the target ("Designed by"). Every place that names a link shows these words, never the relation's code: a record's Traceability section and its facts in the wiki, the side bar's Links out and Links in, the graph's edge labels, legend and connections, the Model view's line titles, and the format reference. An extension that restates a rule may leave them empty to keep the earlier labels, so the rule is reported only when, after every extension is merged, a label is still empty. Write the missing label, in sentence case.
query:
SELECT 'error' AS severity, 'relation-unlabeled' AS "check", NULL AS record,
       'The relation ' || relation || ' from ' || source_kind || ' to ' || target_kind || ' has no '
       || CASE WHEN trim(coalesce(forward_label, '')) = '' AND trim(coalesce(reverse_label, '')) = '' THEN 'forward_label or reverse_label'
               WHEN trim(coalesce(forward_label, '')) = '' THEN 'forward_label'
               ELSE 'reverse_label' END
       || ' in relations.csv; say in plain words what the link means read from '
       || CASE WHEN trim(coalesce(forward_label, '')) = '' AND trim(coalesce(reverse_label, '')) = '' THEN 'each end'
               WHEN trim(coalesce(forward_label, '')) = '' THEN 'the source'
               ELSE 'the target' END
       || ', such as "Satisfies" and "Designed by".' AS message
FROM relations
WHERE relation <> ''
  AND (trim(coalesce(forward_label, '')) = '' OR trim(coalesce(reverse_label, '')) = '')
ORDER BY relation, source_kind, target_kind

name: rule-not-applied
summary: A domain rule that no use case applies.
explanation: A rule that nothing applies is either missing from a use case's `applies` links or no longer needed. Link the use cases that rely on it with `applies`, or remove the rule.
query:
SELECT 'warning' AS severity, 'rule-not-applied' AS "check", r.id AS record,
       'Domain rule ' || r.id || ' is not applied by any use case; link it with "applies" from each use case that relies on it, or remove it.' AS message
FROM records r
WHERE r.kind = 'domain_rule' AND r.id <> ''
  AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM links l JOIN records u ON u.path = l.path
    WHERE l.relation = 'applies' AND l.target = r.id AND u.kind = 'use_case'
  )
ORDER BY record

name: section-stage-mismatch
summary: A kind's section belongs to the kind's own stage.
explanation: A Define kind sits in a Define folder and a Design kind in a Design folder (FORMAT.md section 14). A product-level section, listed with no stage (such as shared), may hold a kind of any stage. Change the kind's `section` or `stage`, or the folder's stage.
query:
SELECT DISTINCT 'error' AS severity, 'section-stage-mismatch' AS "check", NULL AS record,
       'Kind "' || k.kind || '" is in stage "' || coalesce(k.stage, '') || '", but its section "' || k.section
       || '" belongs to stage "' || s.stage || '".' AS message
FROM kinds k
JOIN sections s ON s.section = k.section
WHERE coalesce(s.stage, '') <> ''
  AND coalesce(k.stage, '') <> s.stage
ORDER BY message

name: standard-rule-unmet
summary: A standard rule that nothing meets or cites.
explanation: A standard rule asks nothing of a domain, so it owes no coverage (FORMAT.md section 19), but a rule that no component, design step or test `meets`, and that no other record of its product cites in its prose, has no use, and nothing outlives its purpose. A citation from the rule itself or from its own standard does not count, so a standard that lists its rules by ID does not keep them all alive. A `meets` link from any record counts here; one from a kind the meta-model does not allow is relation-not-allowed. Link what follows the rule with `meets`, cite the rule where it is followed, or remove the rule.
query:
SELECT 'warning' AS severity, 'standard-rule-unmet' AS "check", r.id AS record,
       'Nothing meets or cites standard rule ' || r.id || ' (' || r.title || '). Add meets: [' || r.id
       || '] to a component or test that follows it, cite it where it is followed, or remove it.' AS message
FROM records r
WHERE r.kind = 'standard_rule' AND r.id <> ''
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM links l WHERE l.relation = 'meets' AND l.target = r.id)
  AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM prose_mentions m JOIN records s ON s.id = m.record
    WHERE m.cited = r.id AND m.record <> r.id AND m.record <> coalesce(r.parent, '')
      AND s.product IS NOT DISTINCT FROM r.product
  )
ORDER BY record

name: step-order
summary: A step's order is a whole number that no other step on its path of the flow has, and each path's steps are numbered without gaps.
explanation: The steps of a flow (`flow_step`) and of a technical flow (`design_step`) are read in `order` (FORMAT.md sections 13 and 21), within their `path`: a short name such as main or refused, compared trimmed and in any letter case. A step with no path is on the main path. Orders are compared as numbers, so 1 and 01 clash, and the steps of each path of a flow are numbered 1, 2, 3 and so on. A path whose orders skip a number is reported once, on the first step after the gap, and only when each of its orders is a whole number that no other step of the path has, so one mistake gives one error. A missing order is missing-required-field. Give each step of the path its own whole-number `order`, and close the gap.
query:
SELECT severity, "check", record, message FROM (
WITH all_steps AS (
  SELECT r.path, r.id, r.parent, trim(coalesce(f.value, '')) AS raw,
         -- The step's kind and its flow's, as the meta-model labels them: a "Flow step" in a "flow".
         coalesce(k.label, r.kind) AS label, lower(coalesce(fk.label, sk.flow_kind)) AS flow_label,
         coalesce(nullif(lower(trim(p.value)), ''), 'main') AS step_path,
         CASE WHEN regexp_full_match(trim(f.value), '\d+') THEN TRY_CAST(trim(f.value) AS HUGEINT) END AS n
  FROM records r
  LEFT JOIN (SELECT path, any_value(value) AS value FROM fields WHERE name = 'order' GROUP BY path) f ON f.path = r.path
  LEFT JOIN (SELECT path, any_value(value) AS value FROM fields WHERE name = 'path' GROUP BY path) p ON p.path = r.path
  JOIN (VALUES ('flow_step', 'flow'), ('design_step', 'design_flow')) sk(step_kind, flow_kind) ON sk.step_kind = r.kind
  LEFT JOIN (SELECT kind, any_value(label) AS label FROM kinds GROUP BY kind) k ON k.kind = r.kind
  LEFT JOIN (SELECT kind, any_value(label) AS label FROM kinds GROUP BY kind) fk ON fk.kind = sk.flow_kind
),
steps AS (SELECT * FROM all_steps WHERE raw <> ''),
-- Where a message names the path: nothing for the main path, so a flow with one path reads as before.
named AS (
  SELECT *, CASE WHEN step_path = 'main' THEN '' ELSE ' on path ' || step_path END AS on_path FROM steps
),
-- Each (flow, path) whose steps all have a whole-number order, none repeated: only these are checked for gaps.
clean AS (
  SELECT parent, step_path
  FROM all_steps
  WHERE parent IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY parent, step_path
  HAVING bool_and(n IS NOT NULL) AND count(DISTINCT n) = count(*)
),
gaps AS (
  SELECT s.parent, s.step_path, g.missing
  FROM clean s
  CROSS JOIN LATERAL (
    SELECT m AS missing
    FROM range(1, (SELECT max(n) FROM steps x WHERE x.parent = s.parent AND x.step_path = s.step_path)::BIGINT) t(m)
    WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM steps x WHERE x.parent = s.parent AND x.step_path = s.step_path AND x.n = t.m)
  ) g
)
SELECT 'error' AS severity, 'step-order' AS "check", nullif(s.id, '') AS record,
       s.label || ' ' || coalesce(nullif(s.id, ''), s.path) || ' has order "' || s.raw
       || '", which is not a whole number such as 1 or 2.' AS message
FROM steps s
WHERE s.n IS NULL
UNION ALL
SELECT 'error', 'step-order', nullif(a.id, ''),
       a.label || ' ' || coalesce(nullif(a.id, ''), a.path) || ' has order ' || a.n || a.on_path || ' in ' || a.flow_label || ' ' || a.parent
       || ', the same as ' || string_agg(coalesce(nullif(b.id, ''), b.path), ', ' ORDER BY b.id, b.path)
       || CASE WHEN a.step_path = 'main' THEN '; each step of a ' || a.flow_label || ' needs its own order.'
               ELSE '; each step of a path needs its own order.' END
FROM named a
JOIN named b ON b.parent = a.parent AND b.step_path = a.step_path AND b.n = a.n AND b.path <> a.path
WHERE a.parent IS NOT NULL AND a.n IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY a.id, a.path, a.n, a.parent, a.step_path, a.on_path, a.label, a.flow_label
UNION ALL
SELECT 'error', 'step-order', nullif(s.id, ''),
       s.label || ' ' || coalesce(nullif(s.id, ''), s.path) || ' has order ' || s.n || s.on_path || ' in ' || s.flow_label || ' ' || s.parent
       || ', but no step' || CASE WHEN s.step_path = 'main' THEN '' ELSE ' of that path' END || ' has order '
       || g.missing_list || '; number the steps of '
       || CASE WHEN s.step_path = 'main' THEN 'a ' || s.flow_label ELSE 'a path' END || ' 1, 2, 3 and so on, with no gaps.'
FROM (
  SELECT parent, step_path, min(missing) AS first_missing,
         string_agg(missing::VARCHAR, ', ' ORDER BY missing) AS missing_list
  FROM gaps GROUP BY parent, step_path
) g
JOIN named s ON s.parent = g.parent AND s.step_path = g.step_path
