WHERE s.n = (SELECT min(x.n) FROM steps x WHERE x.parent = g.parent AND x.step_path = g.step_path AND x.n > g.first_missing)
)
ORDER BY record, message

name: test-file-missing
summary: A test's `run_by` file, and its `key_file` when it names one, exists.
explanation: For an automated or manual test a missing file is an error. A planned test may name the file it will live in, so for it a missing file is a warning, as for a component whose file does not exist yet. An automated test with no `run_by` at all is test-run-by-missing. A `key_file` (the file that holds the test's key, when the test runs from a shared class in another file) must be a file under the product root; one outside it is always an error. A key file is read only for a test that names its `run_by`. Fix the path (relative to the repo root), or write the file.
query:
SELECT severity, "check", record, message FROM (
  SELECT CASE WHEN st.state = 'planned' THEN 'warning' ELSE 'error' END AS severity,
         'test-file-missing' AS "check", nullif(f.record, '') AS record, f.path,
         'Test ' || coalesce(nullif(f.record, ''), f.path) || ' is run by ' || f.file || ', which does not exist'
         || CASE WHEN st.state = 'planned' THEN ' yet.' ELSE '.' END AS message
  FROM file_facts f
  LEFT JOIN (SELECT path, max(lower(trim(value))) AS state FROM fields WHERE name = 'state' GROUP BY path) st ON st.path = f.path
  WHERE f.kind = 'test' AND NOT f.file_exists
  UNION ALL
  SELECT CASE WHEN st.state = 'planned' AND f.key_file_inside THEN 'warning' ELSE 'error' END,
         'test-file-missing', nullif(f.record, ''), f.path,
         'Test ' || coalesce(nullif(f.record, ''), f.path) || ' names the key file ' || f.key_file || ', which '
         || CASE WHEN NOT f.key_file_inside THEN 'is outside the product root; name a file under it.'
                 WHEN st.state = 'planned' THEN 'does not exist yet.'
                 ELSE 'does not exist.' END
  FROM file_facts f
  LEFT JOIN (SELECT path, max(lower(trim(value))) AS state FROM fields WHERE name = 'state' GROUP BY path) st ON st.path = f.path
  WHERE f.kind = 'test' AND f.key_file IS NOT NULL AND NOT f.key_file_exists
)
ORDER BY path, message

name: test-file-missing-id
summary: An automated test's `run_by` file names the test, so the code can be traced back to it.
explanation:
The file must name the test's own ID, or else every ID the test proves (each target of a relation whose role is `proof`); a missing proved ID is proof-not-in-file. This check reports the two cases that leave no proved ID to name:

  * a test with a `key` whose file does not contain that key text (the ID rules then do not apply);
  * a test that proves no record and whose file does not name its own ID.

A test that proves no record but `supports` one (a check of a mechanism that backs an obligation without proving it) is not reported: support is never proof, so its file owes no ID. A test with a `key_file` (the file that holds its key, when it runs from a shared class in another file) is judged by that file instead of `run_by`; a key file that is missing or outside the root is test-file-missing only. A test with no state is automated; manual and planned tests are not checked here. Put the test's ID in the test's name in the file, or fix its `key` or `key_file`.
query:
SELECT 'error' AS severity, 'test-file-missing-id' AS "check", nullif(f.record, '') AS record,
       'Test ' || coalesce(nullif(f.record, ''), f.path)
       || CASE WHEN f.key_file IS NOT NULL THEN ' names the key file ' || f.key_file ELSE ' is run by ' || f.file END
       || ', but that file '
       || CASE WHEN k.key IS NOT NULL THEN 'does not contain its key "' || k.key || '".'
               ELSE 'does not mention ' || coalesce(nullif(f.record, ''), 'its ID') || ', and the test proves no record whose ID it could name instead.'
          END AS message
FROM file_facts f
LEFT JOIN (SELECT path, max(trim(value)) AS key FROM fields WHERE name = 'key' AND trim(value) <> '' GROUP BY path) k
       ON k.path = f.path
WHERE f.kind = 'test' AND f.file_exists AND NOT f.contains_id AND f.key_file_exists IS NOT false
  AND coalesce((SELECT max(lower(trim(s.value))) FROM fields s WHERE s.path = f.path AND s.name = 'state'), '')
      NOT IN ('manual', 'planned')
  AND (k.key IS NOT NULL OR (NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM links l
    JOIN records t ON t.id = l.target
    JOIN relations rr ON rr.relation = l.relation AND rr.role = 'proof' AND rr.source_kind = f.kind
                     AND (rr.target_kind = t.kind OR rr.target_kind = '*')
    WHERE l.path = f.path
  ) AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM links l
    JOIN records t ON t.id = l.target
    WHERE l.path = f.path AND l.relation = 'supports'
  )))
ORDER BY f.path

name: test-proves-nothing
summary: A test that proves, and supports, nothing.
explanation: A test exists to prove obligations (a `proof` link such as `proves`) or to check a mechanism that backs one (`supports`). One with neither has no purpose the spec can see: running a flow (`runs`) or exercising a component (`covers`) says what it touches, not what it shows. A link to a record that does not exist does not count (it is only a dangling-link). Link the obligation it proves with "proves", or the one it backs with "supports", or remove the test.
query:
SELECT 'warning' AS severity, 'test-proves-nothing' AS "check", s.id AS record,
       'Test ' || s.id || ' proves nothing and supports nothing; link the obligation it proves with "proves", '
       || 'or the one it backs with "supports", or remove it.' AS message
FROM records s
WHERE s.kind = 'test' AND s.id <> ''
  AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM links l
    JOIN records t ON t.id = l.target
    JOIN relations ro ON ro.relation = l.relation AND ro.source_kind = s.kind AND ro.target_kind IN (t.kind, '*')
                     AND (ro.role = 'proof' OR ro.relation = 'supports')
    WHERE l.path = s.path
  )
ORDER BY record

name: test-run-by-missing
summary: An automated test names the file that runs it in `run_by`.
explanation: A test with no state, or state automated, is automated. Manual and planned tests need no `run_by`. Add the path of the test file, relative to the repo root, or give the test the state it really has.
query:
SELECT 'error' AS severity, 'test-run-by-missing' AS "check", nullif(r.id, '') AS record,
       'Test ' || coalesce(nullif(r.id, ''), r.path) || ' is automated but has no "run_by" naming the file that runs it; '
       || 'name that file, or give the test state manual or planned.' AS message
FROM records r
WHERE r.kind = 'test'
  AND coalesce((SELECT max(lower(trim(s.value))) FROM fields s WHERE s.path = r.path AND s.name = 'state'), '')
      NOT IN ('manual', 'planned')
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM fields s WHERE s.path = r.path AND s.name = 'run_by' AND trim(s.value) <> '')
ORDER BY r.path

name: test-type-mismatch
summary: A test's `test_type` does not suit what it proves.
explanation: Kept conservative: only a test of type domain_rule that proves requirements and no domain rule, or a test of type acceptance that proves domain rules and no requirement, is reported. A unit test may prove either, so it is not reported, nor is any other type, nor a test that proves both. Change the type, or what the test proves.
query:
SELECT 'warning' AS severity, 'test-type-mismatch' AS "check", t.id AS record,
       'Test ' || t.id || ' has test_type ' || t.test_type || ' but proves only '
       || CASE WHEN t.test_type = 'acceptance' THEN 'domain rules' ELSE 'use case requirements' END
       || ' (' || t.targets || '); '
       || CASE WHEN t.test_type = 'acceptance'
               THEN 'an acceptance test proves requirements, so give it test_type domain_rule, or correct what it proves.'
               ELSE 'a domain_rule test proves domain rules, so give it test_type acceptance, or correct what it proves.' END AS message
FROM (
  SELECT r.id, lower(trim(any_value(tt.value))) AS test_type,
         string_agg(DISTINCT l.target, ', ' ORDER BY l.target) AS targets,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE p.kind = 'requirement') AS requirements,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE p.kind = 'domain_rule') AS rules
  FROM records r
  JOIN fields tt ON tt.path = r.path AND tt.name = 'test_type'
  JOIN links l ON l.path = r.path AND l.relation = 'proves'
  JOIN records p ON p.id = l.target
  WHERE r.kind = 'test' AND r.id <> ''
  GROUP BY r.id, r.path
) t
WHERE (t.test_type = 'domain_rule' AND t.requirements > 0 AND t.rules = 0)
   OR (t.test_type = 'acceptance' AND t.rules > 0 AND t.requirements = 0)
ORDER BY record

name: too-many-children
summary: A record with more children of one kind than the product's `structure.maxChildren` setting.
explanation: The setting is read from `lathe.config.json` (default 15) through the settings table. A parent with that many children of one kind is missing a level between them, such as a capability, a layer or another aggregate. Children are counted per kind. Tests are exempt: the app groups them by what they prove (FORMAT.md section 14), so they are never shown as one list. The steps of a flow or a technical flow are counted per path (FORMAT.md sections 13 and 21), since each path reads as its own list, and requirements, interaction requirements, pattern rules and standard rules per `group` (FORMAT.md section 22), since each group reads under its own heading; the ungrouped ones are one list. Groups are compared trimmed and in any letter case. A child whose parent does not exist is only unknown-parent. Add a level, or a group, and move the children into it.
query:
SELECT 'warning' AS severity, 'too-many-children' AS "check", c.parent AS record,
       upper(left(p.kind, 1)) || replace(substr(p.kind, 2), '_', ' ') || ' ' || c.parent || ' has ' || c.n
       || ' children of kind ' || c.kind
       || CASE WHEN c.kind IN ('flow_step', 'design_step') AND c.bucket <> 'main' THEN ' on path ' || c.label
               WHEN c.kind NOT IN ('flow_step', 'design_step') AND c.bucket <> '' THEN ' in group ' || c.label ELSE '' END
       || ', more than the ' || m.max_children
       || ' that structure.maxChildren allows; add a level between them, such as a capability, a layer or another aggregate.' AS message
FROM (
  SELECT r.parent, r.kind,
         -- A step's path (main when it has none); a grouped kind's group (none when it has none); every
         -- other kind is one list.
         CASE WHEN r.kind IN ('flow_step', 'design_step') THEN coalesce(nullif(lower(trim(fp.value)), ''), 'main')
              WHEN r.kind IN ('requirement', 'interaction_requirement', 'pattern_rule', 'standard_rule') THEN lower(trim(coalesce(fg.value, '')))
              ELSE '' END AS bucket,
         -- The path or group as first written.
         min(CASE WHEN r.kind IN ('flow_step', 'design_step') THEN trim(coalesce(fp.value, '')) ELSE trim(coalesce(fg.value, '')) END) AS label,
         count(DISTINCT r.path) AS n
  FROM records r
  LEFT JOIN (SELECT path, any_value(value) AS value FROM fields WHERE name = 'path' GROUP BY path) fp ON fp.path = r.path
  LEFT JOIN (SELECT path, any_value(value) AS value FROM fields WHERE name = 'group' GROUP BY path) fg ON fg.path = r.path
  WHERE r.parent IS NOT NULL AND r.parent <> '' AND r.kind <> 'test'
  GROUP BY r.parent, r.kind, bucket
) c
JOIN (SELECT id, any_value(kind) AS kind FROM records WHERE id <> '' GROUP BY id) p ON p.id = c.parent
CROSS JOIN (SELECT TRY_CAST(any_value(value) AS INTEGER) AS max_children FROM settings WHERE name = 'structure.maxChildren') m
WHERE c.n > m.max_children
ORDER BY record, message

name: undocumented
summary: Every kind, relation and check says what it is, so the format reference documents all of them.
explanation: The reference (`lathe format`, lathe/REFERENCE.md) is generated from the meta-model and the check files, so an empty description or header leaves a hole in it. Reported are a kind with an empty description in `kinds.csv`, a relation rule with an empty description in `relations.csv`, and a check file, Lathe's or the product's, whose header comment lacks a summary sentence, an explanation or a severity line. A check's header is one summary sentence, a blank comment line, the explanation ending with how to fix what it reports, a blank comment line, then `-- severity: error` (or `warning`, or `error, warning`) and an optional `-- kinds: ...` line. Write what is missing.
query:
SELECT 'error' AS severity, 'undocumented' AS "check", NULL AS record, message
FROM (
  SELECT 1 AS part, kind AS name, 'The kind ' || kind || ' has no description in kinds.csv; say in a sentence what a '
         || kind || ' record is.' AS message
  FROM kinds
  WHERE kind <> '' AND trim(coalesce(description, '')) = ''
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 2, relation || ' ' || source_kind || ' ' || target_kind,
         'The relation ' || relation || ' from ' || source_kind || ' to ' || target_kind
         || ' has no description in relations.csv; say in a sentence what the link means.'
  FROM relations
  WHERE relation <> '' AND trim(coalesce(description, '')) = ''
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 3, source,
         'The check ' || source || ' has no ' || replace(missing, ', ', ' or ') || ' in its header comment; start the file with '
         || 'a summary sentence, a blank comment line, the explanation and how to fix it, then a severity line.'
  FROM check_docs
  WHERE missing <> ''
)
ORDER BY part, name

name: unknown-id-in-prose
summary: A record's body cites an ID that no record has.
explanation: A citation is an ID-shaped token with one of the workspace's known prefixes (FORMAT.md section 11). Code spans and fenced code blocks are not read. Fix the wording, or put the ID in code if it is only an example.
query:
SELECT 'warning' AS severity, 'unknown-id-in-prose' AS "check", nullif(m.record, '') AS record,
       coalesce(nullif(m.record, ''), m.path) || ' mentions ' || m.cited || ', which does not exist.' AS message
FROM prose_mentions m
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM records r WHERE r.id = m.cited)
ORDER BY m.record, m.path, m.cited

name: unknown-kind
summary: Every record's kind is one of the kinds the meta-model defines.
explanation: The kinds are Lathe's `meta/kinds.csv` plus any the product adds in its `metaExtensions` folder. A record with a misspelled or missing kind is reported. Fix the `kind` field, or add the kind to the product's `kinds.csv` if it is a kind of its own.
query:
SELECT 'error' AS severity, 'unknown-kind' AS "check", nullif(r.id, '') AS record,
       CASE WHEN r.kind = '' THEN coalesce(nullif(r.id, ''), r.path) || ' has no kind.'
            ELSE coalesce(nullif(r.id, ''), r.path) || ' has kind "' || r.kind || '", which is not a known kind.'
       END AS message
FROM records r
WHERE r.kind NOT IN (SELECT kind FROM kinds)
ORDER BY r.path

name: unknown-parent
summary: A record's parent is a record in the workspace.
explanation: A `parent` that names no record leaves the record outside every product and domain. Fix the ID, or add the missing parent record. A record whose parent does not exist is reported here only, not also by the parent kind check.
query:
SELECT 'error' AS severity, 'unknown-parent' AS "check", nullif(r.id, '') AS record,
       coalesce(nullif(r.id, ''), r.path) || ' names parent ' || r.parent || ', which does not exist.' AS message
FROM records r
WHERE r.parent IS NOT NULL
  AND r.parent NOT IN (SELECT id FROM records)
ORDER BY r.path

name: unknown-relation
summary: Every link uses a relation the meta-model names.
explanation: The relations are Lathe's `meta/relations.csv` plus any the product adds in its extension. A link under a misspelled or unknown relation name is reported once for each record and name. Fix the name under `links`, or add the relation to the product's `relations.csv`.
query:
SELECT DISTINCT 'error' AS severity, 'unknown-relation' AS "check", nullif(l.source, '') AS record,
       coalesce(nullif(l.source, ''), l.path) || ' links to ' || l.target || ' with "' || l.relation || '", which is not a known relation.' AS message
FROM links l
WHERE l.relation NOT IN (SELECT relation FROM relations)
ORDER BY record, message

name: unknown-section
summary: Every section a kind names in `kinds.csv` is a folder that `sections.csv` lists.
explanation: A kind in an unknown folder is shown in no folder of the app (FORMAT.md section 14). Fix the kind's `section`, or add the folder to the product's `sections.csv`.
query:
SELECT DISTINCT 'error' AS severity, 'unknown-section' AS "check", NULL AS record,
       'Kind "' || kind || '" sits in section "' || section || '", which sections.csv does not list.' AS message
FROM kinds
WHERE coalesce(section, '') <> ''
  AND section NOT IN (SELECT section FROM sections)
ORDER BY message

name: unproved
summary: An obligation that no automated or manual test proves yet.
explanation: A test proves an obligation through a `proof` link such as `proves`. A test with no state is automated; a planned test is not proof. A pattern rule is owed by the domains the owed_pattern_rules table names (each domain that follows its pattern, unless the rule is Not applicable or waived there, as in lathe/src/coverage.ts), and only a test in that domain proves it there, so it is reported once for each domain that owes it and lacks one. An automated test's proof counts only when its file backs it, as in coverage: the file names the test's own ID (or its key), or names that target. An unbacked claim is also a proof-not-in-file error. Write a test that `proves` it, and name the test in its file.
query:
SELECT severity, "check", record, message FROM (
WITH stated AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT l.target, t.kind AS target_kind, s.domain AS source_domain, s.kind AS source_kind, s.path,
         coalesce(nullif((SELECT lower(trim(any_value(f.value))) FROM fields f
                          WHERE f.path = s.path AND f.record = s.id AND f.name = 'state'), ''), 'automated') AS state
  FROM links l
  JOIN records s ON s.id = l.source AND s.path = l.path
  JOIN records t ON t.id = l.target
  JOIN relations ro ON ro.role = 'proof' AND ro.relation = l.relation AND ro.source_kind = s.kind
                   AND ro.target_kind IN (t.kind, '*')
),
proof_links AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT target, target_kind, source_domain, state
  FROM stated x
  WHERE x.source_kind <> 'test' OR x.state <> 'automated'
     OR coalesce((SELECT bool_or(f.contains_id) FROM file_facts f WHERE f.path = x.path), false)
     OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM file_mentions m WHERE m.path = x.path AND m.mentioned = x.target)
)
SELECT DISTINCT 'warning' AS severity, 'unproved' AS "check", r.id AS record,
       'No test proves ' || replace(r.kind, '_', ' ') || ' ' || r.id ||
       CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM proof_links x WHERE x.target = r.id AND x.target_kind = r.kind AND x.state = 'planned')
            THEN ' yet: its test is only planned.' ELSE '.' END AS message
FROM records r
WHERE r.id <> ''
  AND r.kind IN (SELECT kind FROM kinds WHERE obligation)
  AND NOT (r.kind = 'pattern_rule' AND r.domain IS NULL)
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM proof_links x WHERE x.target = r.id AND x.target_kind = r.kind
                                               AND x.state IN ('automated', 'manual'))
UNION ALL
SELECT DISTINCT 'warning', 'unproved', o.id,
       'Pattern rule ' || o.id || ' is not proved in ' || o.domain ||
       CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM proof_links x WHERE x.target = o.id AND x.target_kind = o.kind
                                                     AND x.source_domain = o.domain AND x.state = 'planned')
            THEN ' yet: its test there is only planned.'
            ELSE ': no test in ' || o.domain || ' proves it, though the domain follows its pattern.' END
FROM owed_pattern_rules o
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM proof_links x WHERE x.target = o.id AND x.target_kind = o.kind
                                               AND x.source_domain = o.domain AND x.state IN ('automated', 'manual'))
)
ORDER BY record, message

name: unsatisfied
summary: An obligation that no design link targets yet.
explanation: An obligation is any kind the meta-model marks as one. A proof-only obligation kind (kinds.csv obligation `proof`) asks for no design, so it is never reported. A pattern rule is owed by the domains the owed_pattern_rules table names (each domain that follows its pattern, unless the rule is Not applicable or waived there, as in lathe/src/coverage.ts), and only a component in that domain designs it there, so it is reported once for each domain that owes it and lacks one. Link a component to it with `satisfies`, or another design relation.
query:
SELECT severity, "check", record, message FROM (
WITH design_links AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT l.target, t.kind AS target_kind, s.domain AS source_domain
  FROM links l
  JOIN records s ON s.id = l.source AND s.path = l.path
  JOIN records t ON t.id = l.target
  JOIN relations ro ON ro.role = 'design' AND ro.relation = l.relation AND ro.source_kind = s.kind
                   AND ro.target_kind IN (t.kind, '*')
),
owed AS (
  SELECT domain, id, kind FROM owed_pattern_rules
  WHERE kind IN (SELECT kind FROM kinds WHERE obligation AND NOT proof_only)
)
SELECT DISTINCT 'warning' AS severity, 'unsatisfied' AS "check", r.id AS record,
       'Nothing designs ' || replace(r.kind, '_', ' ') || ' ' || r.id || ': no component satisfies it.' AS message
FROM records r
WHERE r.id <> ''
  AND r.kind IN (SELECT kind FROM kinds WHERE obligation AND NOT proof_only)
  AND NOT (r.kind = 'pattern_rule' AND r.domain IS NULL)
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM design_links x WHERE x.target = r.id AND x.target_kind = r.kind)
UNION ALL
SELECT DISTINCT 'warning', 'unsatisfied', o.id,
       'Pattern rule ' || o.id || ' is not designed in ' || o.domain || ': no component in ' || o.domain
       || ' satisfies it, though the domain follows its pattern.'
FROM owed o
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM design_links x WHERE x.target = o.id AND x.target_kind = o.kind
                                                AND x.source_domain = o.domain)
)
ORDER BY record, message

name: use-case-outside-capability
summary: Once a domain has capabilities, each of its use cases sits in one of them.
explanation: A use case left directly under the domain is missing from the domain's use case index. Make one of the domain's capabilities its `parent`; its ID does not change. A domain with no capabilities is not reported.
query:
SELECT 'warning' AS severity, 'use-case-outside-capability' AS "check", u.id AS record,
       'Use case ' || u.id || ' sits directly under domain ' || u.parent
       || ', which has capabilities; move it under the capability it belongs to.' AS message
FROM records u
JOIN records d ON d.id = u.parent AND d.kind = 'domain'
WHERE u.kind = 'use_case' AND u.id <> ''
  AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM records c WHERE c.kind = 'capability' AND c.parent = d.id)
ORDER BY record

name: use-case-without-flow
summary: Once a domain has flows, each of its use cases is carried out by one.
explanation: A flow names the use cases it carries out with `carries_out`. A domain with no flows is not reported: its interaction design has not started. Add the use case to a flow's `carries_out`, or write a flow for it.
query:
SELECT 'warning' AS severity, 'use-case-without-flow' AS "check", u.id AS record,
       'Use case ' || u.id || ' is not carried out by any flow, though domain ' || u.domain
       || ' has flows; link the flow that carries it out with "carries_out".' AS message
FROM records u
WHERE u.kind = 'use_case' AND u.id <> '' AND u.domain IS NOT NULL
  AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM records f WHERE f.kind = 'flow' AND f.domain = u.domain)
  AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM links l JOIN records f ON f.path = l.path
    WHERE l.relation = 'carries_out' AND l.target = u.id AND f.kind = 'flow'
  )
ORDER BY record

name: use-case-without-requirements
summary: A use case with no requirements under it yet.
explanation: A use case's requirements are the rules it must follow, so one with none says nothing checkable. A use case that follows a pattern is left out: its rules come from the pattern's rules, so it may have no requirements of its own. Add `requirement` records under it, or have it follow the pattern it applies.
query:
SELECT DISTINCT 'warning' AS severity, 'use-case-without-requirements' AS "check", u.id AS record,
       'Use case ' || u.id || ' has no requirements.' AS message
FROM records u
WHERE u.kind = 'use_case' AND u.id <> ''
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM records r WHERE r.parent = u.id AND r.kind = 'requirement')
  AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM links l JOIN records p ON p.id = l.target AND p.kind = 'pattern'
    WHERE l.path = u.path AND l.relation = 'follows'
  )
ORDER BY record
